verses.1:1: There was a man from Armathaim Sipha, from Mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeremeel, the son of Elihu, the son of Thoke, in Nasib of Ephraim.
verses.1:2: And he had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no child.
verses.1:3: And the man went up from year to year from his city, from Armathaim, to worship and to sacrifice to the Lord God Sabaoth at Shiloh. And there were Eli and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, priests of the Lord.
verses.1:4: And the day came when Elkanah sacrificed, and he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to her sons;
verses.1:5: and to Hannah he gave one portion, because she had no child, yet Elkanah loved Hannah more than her. And the Lord had closed up her womb,
verses.1:6: because the Lord had not given her a child, according to her affliction and according to the despondency of her affliction. And she was despondent because of this, that the Lord had shut up her womb so as not to give her a child.
verses.1:7: Thus she did year by year when she went up to the house of the Lord; and she was despondent and wept, and did not eat.
verses.1:8: And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah." And she said to him, "Behold, here I am, my lord." And he said to her, "What is the matter with you, that you weep? And why do you not eat? And why does your heart strike you? Am I not better to you than ten children?"
verses.1:9: And she rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and stood before the Lord; and Eli the priest was upon the seat by the doorposts of the temple of the Lord.
verses.1:10: And she was deeply grieved in soul, and prayed to the Lord, speaking, and wept.
verses.1:11: And she vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, "Adonai, Lord Eloi Sabaoth, if You will indeed look upon the lowliness of Your maidservant, and remember me, and give to Your maidservant male offspring, then I will give him before You as a gift until the day of his death; and wine and strong drink he shall not drink, and no iron shall come upon his head."
verses.1:12: And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the Lord, that Eli the priest watched her mouth.
verses.1:13: Now she was speaking in her heart, and her lips were moving, yet her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli considered her to be a drunken woman;
verses.1:14: and the young servant of Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine from yourself, and go out from the presence of the Lord."
verses.1:15: And Hannah answered and said, "No, my lord; I am a woman whose day is hard, and I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I am pouring out my soul before the Lord.
verses.1:16: Do not count your maidservant as a worthless daughter, for out of the abundance of my brooding I have continued until now."
verses.1:17: And Eli answered and said to her, "Go in peace; may the God of Israel grant you every petition of yours which you have asked of Him."
verses.1:18: And she said, "Your maidservant has found favor in your sight." So the woman went her way, and entered into her lodging, and ate with her husband and drank, and her countenance was no longer downcast.
verses.1:19: And they rose early in the morning and worshiped the Lord, and went their way. And Elkanah entered into his house at Armathaim, and he knew Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her.
verses.1:20: And she conceived, and it came to pass in the course of time that she bore a son; and she called his name Samuel, and said, "Because I have asked for him from the Lord God Sabaoth."
verses.1:21: And the man Elkanah and all his house went up to offer in Shiloh the yearly sacrifice, and his vows, and all the tithes of his land.
verses.1:22: But Hannah did not go up with him, for she said to her husband, "Not until the child goes up, when I have weaned him; then he shall appear before the face of the Lord, and abide there forever."
verses.1:23: And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what is good in your sight; remain until you have weaned him; only may the Lord establish what has gone forth from your mouth." So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.
verses.1:24: And she went up with him to Shiloh with a three-year-old calf, and loaves of bread, and an ephah of fine flour, and a skin of wine. And she entered into the house of the Lord in Shiloh, and the child was with them.
verses.1:25: And they brought him before the Lord, and his father slaughtered the sacrifice which he offered from year to year to the Lord. And he brought the child forward and slaughtered the calf; and Hannah, the mother of the child, brought him to Eli,
verses.1:26: and said, "Oh, my lord! As your soul lives, I am the woman who stood before you, with you, when praying to the Lord.
verses.1:27: For this child I prayed, and the Lord has granted my petition which I asked of Him.
verses.1:28: Therefore I also lend him to the Lord all the days that he lives, as a loan to the Lord." And she said:
verses.2:1: "My heart has been established in the Lord; my horn has been exalted in my God. My mouth has been opened wide against enemies; I have rejoiced in Your salvation.
verses.2:2: For there is none holy like the Lord, and there is none righteous like our God; there is none holy besides You.
verses.2:3: Do not boast, and do not speak lofty things; do not let arrogant speech come out of your mouth; for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and a God who prepares His own deeds.
verses.2:4: The bow of the mighty has grown weak, and those who are weak have girded themselves with strength.
verses.2:5: Those who were full of bread have been brought low, and those who were weak have forsaken the land. For the barren woman has borne seven, and she who had many children has grown weak.
verses.2:6: The Lord puts to death and makes alive; He brings down to Hades and brings up.
verses.2:7: The Lord makes poor and makes rich; He brings low and lifts up.
verses.2:8: He raises the needy from the earth, and lifts the poor from the dunghill, to seat him with the princes of the peoples, and causing them to inherit a throne of glory;
verses.2:9: granting his vow to the one who vows, and He has blessed the years of the righteous. For by strength no man is mighty.
verses.2:10: The Lord will make His adversary weak; the Lord is holy. Do not let the prudent man boast in his prudence, and do not let the mighty man boast in his might, and do not let the rich man boast in his riches; rather, let him who boasts boast in this: to understand and know the Lord, and to execute judgment and righteousness in the midst of the earth. The Lord ascended into the heavens and thundered; He Himself will judge the ends of the earth. And He gives strength to our kings, and He will exalt the horn of His anointed."
verses.2:11: And she left him there before the Lord, and departed to Armathaim. And the child was ministering before the face of the Lord in the presence of Eli the priest.
verses.2:12: Now the sons of Eli the priest were worthless sons, who did not know the Lord.
verses.2:13: And this was the priest's due from all the people who offered sacrifice: the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fleshhook in his hand,
verses.2:14: and he would thrust it into the great cauldron, or into the copper kettle, or into the pot; whatever came up on the fleshhook, the priest would take for himself. In this manner they did to all Israel who came to sacrifice to the Lord in Shiloh.
verses.2:15: Also, before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give meat to roast for the priest, for I will by no means take boiled meat from you out of the cauldron."
verses.2:16: And the man who was sacrificing would say, "Let the fat be burned first, as is fitting, and then take for yourself from all that your soul desires." And he said, "No, for you shall give it now; and if not, I will take it by force."
verses.2:17: Therefore the sin of the young servants was exceedingly great before the Lord, for they despised the sacrifice of the Lord.
verses.2:18: Now Samuel was ministering before the Lord, a child girded with a linen ephod.
verses.2:19: And his mother made him a little robe, and brought it up to him from year to year when she went up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
verses.2:20: And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May the Lord repay you with offspring from this woman in place of the loan which you lent to the Lord." And the man departed to his own place.
verses.2:21: And the Lord visited Hannah, and she bore yet three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew great before the Lord.
verses.2:22: Now Eli was exceedingly old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel;
verses.2:23: and he said to them, "Why do you do according to this thing which I hear from the mouth of all the people of the Lord?
verses.2:24: No, children, for the report which I hear is not good; do not do so, for the reports which I hear are not good, so that the people do not serve God.
verses.2:25: If a man indeed sins against a man, then they will pray for him to the Lord; but if he sins against the Lord, who shall pray for him?" Yet they did not listen to the voice of their father, because the Lord indeed purposed to destroy them.
verses.2:26: And the child Samuel walked on, and was good both with the Lord and with men.
verses.2:27: And a man of God came to Eli and said, "Thus says the Lord: I plainly revealed Myself to the house of your father when they were in the land of Egypt, servants to the house of Pharaoh;
verses.2:28: and I chose the house of your father out of all the tribes of Israel to serve as priests to Me, and to go up upon My altar, and to burn incense, and to bear an ephod; and I gave to the house of your father all the fire offerings of the sons of Israel for food.
verses.2:29: And why have you looked upon My incense and upon My sacrifice with a shameless eye, and glorified your sons above Me, to bless yourselves with the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel before Me?
verses.2:30: Therefore thus has the Lord God of Israel said: I said, 'Your house and the house of your father shall walk before Me forever.' Yet now the Lord declares: Far be it from Me! For rather, those who glorify Me I will glorify, and he who despises Me shall be dishonored.
verses.2:31: Behold, days are coming when I will utterly destroy your seed and the seed of your father's house,
verses.2:32: and you shall not have an old man in My house all the days.
verses.2:33: And a man I will not utterly destroy from My altar, that his eyes may fail and his soul may waste away; and every survivor of your house shall fall by the sword of men.
verses.2:34: And this shall be the sign to you that shall come upon these two sons of yours, Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall both die.
verses.2:35: And I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest, who shall do all the things that are in My heart and in My soul; and I will build him a faithful house, and he shall walk before My anointed all the days.
verses.2:36: And it shall come to pass that whoever remains in the house shall come to bow down to him for an obol of silver, saying, 'Cast me into one of your priestly offices, to eat bread.'"
verses.3:1: Now the boy Samuel was ministering to the Lord before Eli the priest. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no distinct vision.
verses.3:2: And it came to pass on that day that Eli was sitting in his place, and his eyes had begun to grow heavy, and he could not see.
verses.3:3: And before the lamp of God was trimmed, Samuel was sleeping in the temple, where the ark of God was.
verses.3:4: And the Lord called, "Samuel, Samuel!" And he said, "Here I am."
verses.3:5: And he ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you have called me." And he said, "I have not called you; return and sleep." So he returned and went to sleep.
verses.3:6: And the Lord called yet again, "Samuel, Samuel!" And he went to Eli a second time and said, "Here I am, for you have called me." And he said, "I have not called you; return and sleep."
verses.3:7: Now Samuel did not yet know God, nor had the word of the Lord yet been revealed to him.
verses.3:8: And the Lord called Samuel a third time; and he arose and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you have called me." Then Eli discerned that the Lord had called the boy.
verses.3:9: And he said, "Return and sleep, child; and it shall be, if He calls you, that you shall say, 'Speak, for Your servant hears.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
verses.3:10: And the Lord came and stood, and called him as once and again. And Samuel said, "Speak, for Your servant hears."
verses.3:11: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Behold, I am performing My words in Israel; of everyone who hears them, both his ears shall ring.
verses.3:12: In that day I will raise up against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house; I will begin and I will bring it to completion.
verses.3:13: And I have declared to him that I am executing vengeance upon his house forever for the iniquities of his sons, because his sons were reviling God, and he did not admonish them,
verses.3:14: not even so. I have sworn to the house of Eli, 'The iniquity of the house of Eli shall by no means be atoned for with incense and with sacrifices forever.'"
verses.3:15: And Samuel lay until morning, and he rose early in the morning and opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel was afraid to declare the vision to Eli.
verses.3:16: And Eli said to Samuel, "Samuel, child." And he said, "Here I am."
verses.3:17: And he said, "What is the word that was spoken to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do so to you if you hide from me a single word of all the words that were spoken to you in your ears."
verses.3:18: So Samuel declared all the words and hid nothing from him. And Eli said, "He is the Lord; He will do what is good in His sight."
verses.3:19: And Samuel grew up, and the Lord was with him, and none of all his words fell to the ground.
verses.3:20: And all Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was trustworthy as a prophet to the Lord.
verses.3:21: And the Lord continued to be made known in Shiloh, for the Lord was revealed to Samuel; and Samuel was accredited to be a prophet to the Lord for all Israel from one end of the land even to the other. Now Eli was exceedingly old, and his sons kept going on, and their way was wicked before the Lord.
verses.4:1: And it came to pass in those days that foreigners gathered together for war against Israel; and Israel went out to meet them for battle, and they encamped at Ebenezer, while the foreigners encamped in Aphek.
verses.4:2: And the foreigners drew up in battle array against Israel. And the battle turned, and the men of Israel were defeated before the foreigners, and four thousand men were struck down in the battle line in the field.
verses.4:3: And the people came into the camp, and the elders of Israel said, "Why has the Lord defeated us today before the foreigners? Let us take the ark of our God from Shiloh, and let it go forth from our midst, and it shall save you from the hand of our enemies."
verses.4:4: So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the Lord who is enthroned upon the cherubim. And both of the sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were with the ark.
verses.4:5: And it came to pass, when the ark of the Lord came into the camp, that all Israel shouted with a loud voice, and the earth resounded.
verses.4:6: And the foreigners heard the cry, and the foreigners said, "What is this great cry in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they learned that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.
verses.4:7: And the foreigners were afraid and said, "These gods have come to them in the camp! Woe to us! Deliver us, O Lord, today, for such a thing has not happened yesterday or the day before.
verses.4:8: Woe to us! Who shall deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague and in the wilderness.
verses.4:9: Be strong and be men, and fight against them!"
verses.4:10: So they fought against them, and the men of Israel were defeated, and every man fled to his tent. And there was an exceedingly great slaughter, and thirty thousand of the ranks of Israel fell.
verses.4:11: And the ark of God was captured, and both of the sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
verses.4:12: And a Jeminite man ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh on that day, with his garments torn and earth upon his head.
verses.4:13: And he came, and behold, Eli was on his seat beside the gate, watching the road, for his heart was in great anxiety concerning the ark of God. And the man entered the city to tell the news, and the city cried out aloud.
verses.4:14: And Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, "What is the outcry of this sound?" And the man made haste, came in, and reported to Eli.
verses.4:15: Now Eli was ninety years old, and his eyes were fixed so that he could not see. And Eli said to the men who were standing around him, "What is the sound of this uproar?"
verses.4:16: And the man made haste, came up to Eli, and said to him, "I am the one who has come from the camp, and I have fled from the battle line today." And he said, "What is the thing that has happened, child?"
verses.4:17: And the young man answered and said, "The men of Israel have fled before the foreigners, and there has been a great slaughter among the people, and both of your sons have died, and the ark of God has been captured."
verses.4:18: And it came to pass, when he made mention of the ark of God, that he fell backward from the seat beside the gate, and his back was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel twenty years.
verses.4:19: Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was with child, near the time to give birth; and she heard the report that the ark of God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, and she wept and gave birth, for her labor pains came upon her.
verses.4:20: And in her hour she was dying. And the women who stood beside her said to her, "Do not fear, for you have borne a son." But she did not answer, nor did her heart take heed.
verses.4:21: And she named the boy Woe Barchaboth, on account of the ark of God, and on account of her father-in-law, and on account of her husband.
verses.4:22: And they said, "The glory of Israel has been carried into exile, because the ark of the Lord has been captured."
verses.5:1: And the foreigners took the ark of God and brought it from Abenner to Ashdod.
verses.5:2: And the foreigners took the ark of the Lord and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.
verses.5:3: And the Ashdodites rose early and entered the house of Dagon, and they looked, and behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of God. And they lifted Dagon up and set him in his place. And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the Ashdodites, and He tormented them and struck them in their secret parts, both Ashdod and its borders.
verses.5:4: And it came to pass, when they rose early in the morning, that behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the covenant of the Lord; and the head of Dagon and both palms of his hands were severed, each of them upon the front of the threshold, and both wrists of his hands had fallen upon the porch; only the spine of Dagon was left.
verses.5:5: Therefore the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters the house of Dagon do not tread upon the threshold of the house of Dagon in Ashdod to this day, because they always step right over it.
verses.5:6: And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon Ashdod, and He brought affliction upon them, and it broke out upon them in the ships, and in the midst of its land mice sprang up; and there was a great deadly confusion in the city.
verses.5:7: And the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, and they said, "The ark of God shall not remain with us, for His hand is harsh upon us and upon Dagon our god."
verses.5:8: And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners to themselves and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And the Gittites said, "Let the ark of God come over to us." So the ark of God went over to Gath.
verses.5:9: And it came to pass after it had gone over, that the hand of the Lord came upon the city with an exceedingly great tumult; and He struck the men of the city from small to great, and He struck them in their secret parts. And the Gittites made seats for themselves.
verses.5:10: And they sent away the ark of God to Ashkelon. And it came to pass, as the ark of God entered Ashkelon, that the Ashkelonites cried out, saying, "Why have you turned the ark of the God of Israel back to us, to put us and our people to death?"
verses.5:11: So they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners and said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it settle in its own place, so that it may by no means put us and our people to death." For an exceedingly heavy confusion had come upon the whole city when the ark of the God of Israel entered there.
verses.5:12: And those who lived and did not die were struck in their secret parts; and the outcry of the city ascended to heaven.
verses.6:1: And the ark was in the country of the Philistines seven months, and their land swarmed with mice.
verses.6:2: And the Philistines called their priests, their diviners, and their enchanters, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of the Lord? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place."
verses.6:3: And they said, "If you send away the ark of the covenant of God, the Lord of Israel, do not send it away empty, but by all means render to it an offering for the torment; then you shall be healed, and atonement shall be made for you. Will His hand not depart from you?"
verses.6:4: And they said, "What offering for the torment shall we render to it?" And they said, "According to the number of the lords of the Philistines, five golden seats, because a calamity is among you, and your rulers, and the people,
verses.6:5: and golden mice, the likeness of your mice that are destroying the land. And you shall give glory to the Lord, so that He may lighten His hand from you, and from your gods, and from your land.
verses.6:6: And why do you harden your hearts, as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their heart? When He mocked them, did they not send them away, and they departed?
verses.6:7: Now therefore, take and make a new cart, and take two cows that have borne their first young, without their young; and yoke the cows to the cart, and lead their young away from behind them back home.
verses.6:8: And you shall take the ark and set it upon the cart, and the golden articles you shall render to it for the torment, and you shall not put them in a berechthan coffer at its side; and you shall send it away and drive it off, and you shall depart.
verses.6:9: And watch: if it goes along the way to its own border toward Beth-shemesh, He has done this great evil to us; but if not, then we shall know that His hand has not touched us, but this has happened to us by chance."
verses.6:10: And the Philistines did so; they took two cows that had borne their first young and yoked them to the cart, and kept their young back at home.
verses.6:11: And they set the ark upon the cart, and the ergab coffer, and the golden mice.
verses.6:12: And the cows went straight along the road toward the way of Beth-shemesh; they walked along one path and toiled on, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the lords of the Philistines walked behind it as far as the borders of Beth-shemesh.
verses.6:13: Now those in Beth-shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark of the Lord, and rejoiced to meet it.
verses.6:14: And the cart came into the field of Hosea, which was in Beth-shemesh, and they set up a great stone there beside it; and they split the wood of the cart and offered up the cows as a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.6:15: And the Levites brought up the ark of the Lord, and the ergab coffer with it, and the golden articles that were upon it, and set them upon the great stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrifices to the Lord on that day.
verses.6:16: And the five lords of the Philistines saw it, and returned to Ashkelon on that day.
verses.6:17: And these are the golden seats which the Philistines rendered to the Lord for the torment: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron;
verses.6:18: and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, from the fortified city even to the village of the Perizzite, and as far as the great stone on which they placed the ark of the covenant of the Lord, which is in the field of Hosea the Beth-shemite.
verses.6:19: And the sons of Jeconiah were not pleased with the men of Beth-shemesh, because they saw the ark of the Lord; and He struck among them seventy men and fifty thousand men. And the people mourned, because the Lord had struck the people with an exceedingly great plague.
verses.6:20: And the men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who shall be able to pass before this holy One? And to whom shall the ark of the Lord go up from us?"
verses.6:21: So they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "The Philistines have returned the ark of the Lord; come down and bring it up to yourselves."
verses.7:1: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought up the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and brought it into the house of Amminadab on the hill; and they sanctified Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.7:2: And it came to pass from the day that the ark was in Kiriath-jearim that the days multiplied and became twenty years; and all the house of Israel looked after the Lord.
verses.7:3: Then Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, "If you are returning to the Lord with all your heart, put away the foreign gods from among you, and the groves, and prepare your hearts for the Lord, and serve Him alone; and He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:4: So the children of Israel put away the Baals and the groves of Ashtaroth, and served the Lord alone.
verses.7:5: And Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you."
verses.7:6: And they gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water and poured it out before the Lord upon the ground. And they fasted on that day, and said, "We have sinned before the Lord." And Samuel judged the children of Israel at Mizpah.
verses.7:7: Now when the Philistines heard that all the children of Israel had gathered together to Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And the children of Israel heard of it, and were afraid before the Philistines.
verses.7:8: And the children of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not remain silent on our behalf from crying out to the Lord your God, and He will save us from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:9: And Samuel took one suckling lamb and offered it as a burnt offering to the Lord with all the people; and Samuel cried out to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him.
verses.7:10: Now as Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel; and the Lord thundered with a loud voice on that day against the Philistines, and they were thrown into confusion and defeated before Israel.
verses.7:11: And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.
verses.7:12: Then Samuel took one stone and set it up between Mizpah and the Old, and called its name Ebenezer, Stone of the Helper, and said, "Thus far the Lord has helped us."
verses.7:13: And the Lord humbled the Philistines, and they did not come anymore into the territory of Israel; and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
verses.7:14: And the cities which the Philistines had taken from the children of Israel were restored, and they restored them to Israel from Ashkelon to Azob, and they took back the territory of Israel from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
verses.7:15: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
verses.7:16: He went from year to year on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and judged Israel in all these sanctified places.
verses.7:17: And his return was to Ramathaim, for his house was there; and there he judged Israel, and there he built an altar to the Lord.
verses.8:1: Now it came to pass when Samuel grew old that he appointed his sons as judges for Israel.
verses.8:2: And these were the names of his sons: the firstborn, Joel, and the name of the second, Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba.
verses.8:3: Yet his sons did not walk in his way, but turned aside after profit, and took bribes, and perverted justice.
verses.8:4: Then the men of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramathaim,
verses.8:5: and said to him, "Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your way. Now therefore, appoint for us a king to judge us like the rest of the nations."
verses.8:6: And the matter was evil in the eyes of Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." So Samuel prayed to the Lord.
verses.8:7: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Heed the voice of the people in whatever they speak to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them.
verses.8:8: According to all the deeds which they have done to Me from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, in that they forsook Me and served other gods, so they are doing to you also.
verses.8:9: Now therefore, heed their voice; yet you shall solemnly testify to them, and declare to them the right of the king who shall reign over them."
verses.8:10: So Samuel spoke every word of the Lord to the people who were asking a king from him.
verses.8:11: And he said, "This shall be the right of the king who shall reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them for his chariots and for his horsemen, and some to run before his chariots;
verses.8:12: and he will appoint them for himself as commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and to reap his harvest and gather his vintage, and to make his instruments of war and equipment for his chariots.
verses.8:13: And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, and cooks, and bakers.
verses.8:14: And he will take your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves that are good, and give them to his servants.
verses.8:15: And he will take a tenth of your seed and your vineyards, and give it to his eunuchs and to his servants.
verses.8:16: And he will take your male servants, your female servants, your herds and your good things, and your donkeys, and take a tenth for his own work.
verses.8:17: And he will take a tenth of your flocks; and you yourselves shall be his servants.
verses.8:18: And you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves; and the Lord will not hear you in those days, because you yourselves have chosen a king for yourselves."
verses.8:19: Nevertheless the people refused to listen to Samuel; and they said to him, "No, but a king shall be over us,
verses.8:20: that we also may be like all the nations, and our king shall judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battle."
verses.8:21: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and spoke them in the ears of the Lord.
verses.8:22: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Heed their voice, and make them a king." And Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Let every man return to his own city."
verses.9:1: Now there was a man of the sons of Benjamin, and his name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Ared, the son of Bachi, the son of Aphek, the son of a Jeminite man, a mighty man.
verses.9:2: And he had a son, and his name was Saul, a man of great stature, a goodly man; and among the sons of Israel there was no one more goodly than he—from the shoulders and upward he was taller than all the land.
verses.9:3: Now the donkeys of Kish, the father of Saul, were lost; and Kish said to Saul his son, "Take one of the young servants with you, and arise, go, and seek the donkeys."
verses.9:4: So they passed through the hill country of Ephraim and passed through the land of Selcha, and they did not find them; then they passed through the land of Easakem, and they were not there; and they passed through the land of Jakim, and they did not find them.
verses.9:5: When they came to Seiph, Saul said to his young servant who was with him, "Come, and let us return, lest my father cease caring about the donkeys and become anxious for us."
verses.9:6: And the young servant said to him, "Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is held in honor; everything that he speaks will surely come to pass. Now therefore let us go, so that he may tell us our way on which we have gone."
verses.9:7: Then Saul said to his young servant who was with him, "And behold, we will go, yet what shall we bring to the man of God? For the loaves of bread are spent from our vessels, and there is nothing more with us of what we possess to bring to the man of God."
verses.9:8: And the young servant answered Saul again and said, "Behold, there is found in my hand a fourth part of a shekel of silver; and you shall give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."
verses.9:9: Now formerly in Israel, each man spoke thus when he went to inquire of God: "Come, let us go to the seer"; for formerly the people called the prophet "the Seer."
verses.9:10: Then Saul said to his young servant, "The word is good; come, and let us go." So they went to the city where the man of God was.
verses.9:11: As they went up the ascent of the city, they found maidens going out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer here?"
verses.9:12: And the maidens answered them and said to them, "He is; behold, he is right before you. Now because of the day he has come into the city, for the people have a sacrifice today in Bama.
verses.9:13: As soon as you enter the city, you will at once find him in the city before he goes up to Bama to eat; for the people will by no means eat until he enters, because he blesses the sacrifice, and afterward the guests eat. Now therefore go up, for because of the day you will find him."
verses.9:14: So they went up to the city. As they were entering into the midst of the city, behold, Samuel came out to meet them, to go up to Bama.
verses.9:15: Now the Lord had uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came to him, saying,
verses.9:16: "About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as ruler over My people Israel, and he shall save My people from the hand of the foreigners; for I have looked upon the affliction of My people, because their cry has come to Me."
verses.9:17: And Samuel saw Saul, and the Lord answered him, "Behold the man of whom I spoke to you! This one shall rule over My people."
verses.9:18: Then Saul drew near to Samuel in the midst of the city and said, "Please tell me, which is the house of the seer?"
verses.9:19: And Samuel answered Saul and said, "I am he. Go up before me to Bama and eat with me today, and in the morning I will send you away and will tell you all that is in your heart.
verses.9:20: And concerning your donkeys that were lost three days ago today, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And for whom are the choice things of Israel? Are they not for you and for the house of your father?"
verses.9:21: And Saul answered and said, "Am I not the son of a Jeminite man, of the small tribe of the stock of Israel, and of the least clan of the whole tribe of Benjamin? Why then have you spoken to me according to this word?"
verses.9:22: Then Samuel took Saul and his young servant and brought them into the guest hall, and set a place for them there among the foremost of those who were invited, about seventy men.
verses.9:23: And Samuel said to the cook, "Give me the portion which I gave you, of which I told you to set it aside with you."
verses.9:24: So the cook boiled the thigh and set it before Saul; and Samuel said to Saul, "Behold what has been left over; set it before yourself and eat, for as a testimony it has been set for you above the others—cut off pieces." So Saul ate with Samuel on that day.
verses.9:25: And he came down from Bama into the city; and they spread a bed for Saul on the housetop, and he lay down to sleep.
verses.9:26: And it came to pass, as the dawn was rising, that Samuel called to Saul on the housetop, saying, "Arise, and I will send you away." So Saul arose, and both he and Samuel went outside.
verses.9:27: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, "Speak to the young man, and let him pass on ahead of us; and you, stand still just now, and hear the word of God."
verses.10:1: Then Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it upon his head, and kissed him and said to him, "Has not the Lord anointed you as ruler over His people, over Israel? And you shall rule over the people of the Lord, and you shall save them from the hand of their enemies all around. And this shall be the sign to you that the Lord has anointed you over His inheritance as ruler:
verses.10:2: when you depart from me today, you will find two men by the tombs of Rachel in the hill country of Benjamin, leaping greatly, and they will say to you, 'The donkeys which you went to seek have been found; and behold, your father has shaken off the matter of the donkeys and is greatly anxious about you, saying, "What shall I do for my son?"'
verses.10:3: Then you shall go on from there and come farther, as far as the oak of Tabor, and there you will find three men going up to God at Bethel: one carrying three young goats, and one carrying three vessels of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine.
verses.10:4: And they will ask after your peace and will give you two firstfruits of bread, and you shall receive them from their hand.
verses.10:5: After that you shall enter the hill of God, where the garrison of the foreigners is—there is Nasib the foreigner. And it shall be, when you enter there into the city, that you will meet a company of prophets coming down from Bama, and before them a harp, a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre, and they will be prophesying.
verses.10:6: And the Spirit of the Lord will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.
verses.10:7: And it shall be, when these signs come upon you, do whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.
verses.10:8: And you shall go down before Gilead; and behold, I am coming down to you to offer up a burnt offering and peace sacrifices. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do."
verses.10:9: And it came to pass, as he turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel, that God changed his heart into another heart; and all the signs came to pass on that day.
verses.10:10: And he came from there to the hill, and behold, a company of prophets came toward him; and the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.
verses.10:11: And it happened that all who knew him yesterday and the day before saw him, and behold, he was in the midst of the prophets. Then the people said, each man to his neighbor, "What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:12: And one of them answered and said, "And who is his father?" Therefore it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:13: And when he had finished prophesying, he came to the hill.
verses.10:14: Then his kinsman said to him and to his young servant, "Where did you go?" And they said, "To seek the donkeys; and we saw that they were not there, so we went in to Samuel."
verses.10:15: And the kinsman said to Saul, "Please tell me what Samuel said to you."
verses.10:16: And Saul said to his kinsman, "He plainly told me that the donkeys had been found." But the matter of the kingdom he did not tell him.
verses.10:17: Then Samuel summoned all the people to the Lord at Mizpah,
verses.10:18: and said to the sons of Israel, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: 'I brought up the sons of Israel out of Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt and from all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.'
verses.10:19: Yet today you have rejected God, who Himself is your Savior from all your evils and your afflictions, and you have said, 'No, rather you shall set a king over us.' Now therefore present yourselves before the Lord according to your tribes and according to your clans."
verses.10:20: So Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken by lot.
verses.10:21: Then he brought near the tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and the clan of Mattari was taken by lot; and they brought near the clan of Mattari man by man, and Saul the son of Kish was taken by lot. And he sought him, but he was not found.
verses.10:22: Therefore Samuel inquired further of the Lord, "Is the man coming here?" And the Lord said, "Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage."
verses.10:23: So he ran and took him from there, and set him in the midst of the people; and he stood taller than all the people from the shoulders and upward.
verses.10:24: And Samuel said to all the people, "Have you seen him whom the Lord has chosen for Himself, that there is none like him among all of you?" And all the people recognized him and said, "Let the king live!"
verses.10:25: Then Samuel spoke to the people the ordinance of the king, and wrote it in a book and laid it before the Lord. And Samuel sent all the people away, and each man departed to his own place.
verses.10:26: And Saul also departed to his house at Gibeah; and men of valor whose hearts the Lord had touched went with Saul.
verses.10:27: But pestilent men said, "How shall this man save us?" And they despised him and brought him no gifts.
verses.11:1: And it came to pass, about a month later, that Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh Gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash the Ammonite, "Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you."
verses.11:2: And Nahash the Ammonite said to them, "On this condition I will make a covenant with you: by gouging out every right eye among you, and I will lay a reproach upon Israel."
verses.11:3: And the men of Jabesh said to him, "Grant us seven days, and we will send messengers into all the territory of Israel; and if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you."
verses.11:4: Then the messengers came to Gibeah to Saul and spoke the words in the ears of the people; and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.11:5: And behold, Saul was coming after the morning from the field; and Saul said, "Why is it that the people are weeping?" And they related to him the words of the sons of Jabesh.
verses.11:6: Then the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his wrath was exceedingly kindled against them.
verses.11:7: And he took two oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them into all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, "Whoever does not go out after Saul and after Samuel, thus shall they do to his oxen." And the dread of the Lord came upon the people of Israel, and they cried out as one man.
verses.11:8: And he inspected them at Abiezek in Bama: every man of Israel, six hundred thousand, and the men of Judah, seventy thousand.
verses.11:9: And he said to the messengers who had come, "Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh: 'Tomorrow deliverance shall be yours when the sun grows hot.'" So the messengers came into the city and reported it to the men of Jabesh, and they rejoiced.
verses.11:10: Therefore the men of Jabesh said to Nahash the Ammonite, "Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you shall do to us whatever is good in your sight."
verses.11:11: And it came to pass on the next day that Saul divided the people into three companies; and they entered the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and struck down the sons of Ammon until the day grew hot. And it happened that those who remained were scattered, so that not two of them were left together.
verses.11:12: Then the people said to Samuel, "Who is he who said that Saul shall not reign over us? Deliver up the men, and we will put them to death."
verses.11:13: But Samuel said, "No one shall be put to death on this day, for today the Lord has accomplished deliverance in Israel."
verses.11:14: Then Samuel said to the people, "Let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there."
verses.11:15: So all the people went to Gilgal, and Samuel anointed Saul there as king before the Lord in Gilgal, and he offered there sacrifices and peace offerings before the Lord; and Samuel and all Israel rejoiced exceedingly.
verses.12:1: And Samuel said to all Israel, "Behold, I have listened to your voice in all things that you have said to me, and I have set a king to reign over you.
verses.12:2: And now, behold, the king goes about before you, while I have grown old and shall sit; and behold, my sons are among you. And behold, I have walked before you from youth even to this day.
verses.12:3: Behold, here I am; testify against me before the Lord and before His anointed. Whose calf have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or whom of you have I oppressed, or whom have I crushed, or from whose hand have I taken a bribe and a sandal? Testify against me, and I will restore it to you."
verses.12:4: And they said to Samuel, "You have not wronged us, nor have you oppressed or crushed us, and you have not taken anything from anyone's hand."
verses.12:5: And Samuel said to the people, "The Lord is witness among you, and His anointed is witness today, on this day, that you have not found anything in my hand." And they said, "He is witness."
verses.12:6: And Samuel spoke to the people, saying, "The Lord is witness, who made Moses and Aaron, who brought our fathers up out of Egypt.
verses.12:7: And now, take your stand, and I will judge you before the Lord, and I will declare to you all the righteousness of the Lord—the deeds He performed among you and among your fathers:
verses.12:8: how Jacob and his sons entered into Egypt, and Egypt humbled them; and our fathers cried out to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought our fathers out of Egypt, and He settled them in this place.
verses.12:9: And they forgot the Lord their God, and He sold them into the hands of Sisera, commander of the army of Jabis king of Hazor, and into the hands of foreigners, and into the hands of the king of Moab, and he waged war against them.
verses.12:10: And they cried out to the Lord and said, 'We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord and have served the Baals and the groves; and now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve You.'
verses.12:11: And He sent Jeroboam and Barak and Jephthah and Samuel, and He delivered you from the hand of your enemies all around, and you dwelt in safety.
verses.12:12: And you saw that Nahash, king of the sons of Ammon, came against you, and you said, 'No, rather a king shall reign over us.'
verses.12:13: And now, behold the king whom you have chosen; and behold, the Lord has given a king over you.
verses.12:14: If you fear the Lord and serve Him, and listen to His voice, and do not contend against the mouth of the Lord, then both you and the king who reigns over you shall continue walking after the Lord.
verses.12:15: But if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord, and contend against the mouth of the Lord, then the hand of the Lord shall be against you and against your king.
verses.12:16: And now, take your stand and see this great thing which the Lord will do before your eyes.
verses.12:17: Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call upon the Lord, and He will give thunder and rain; and know and see that your wickedness is great, which you have done before the Lord in asking for a king for yourselves."
verses.12:18: And Samuel called upon the Lord, and the Lord gave thunder and rain on that day; and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.
verses.12:19: And all the people said to Samuel, "Pray for your servants to the Lord your God, that we may not die; for we have added wickedness to all our sins, in asking for a king for ourselves."
verses.12:20: And Samuel said to the people, "Do not fear. You have done all this wickedness; yet do not turn aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart.
verses.12:21: And do not go astray after things that are nothing, which will accomplish nothing and will not deliver, for they are nothing.
verses.12:22: For the Lord will not cast off His people for the sake of His great name, because the Lord has graciously taken you to Himself as a people.
verses.12:23: And as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the Lord by ceasing to pray for you; and I will serve the Lord, and I will show you the good and straight way.
verses.12:24: Only fear the Lord and serve Him in truth and with all your heart, for you have seen what great things He has done with you.
verses.12:25: And if in wickedness you persist in doing evil, both you and your king shall be gathered away."
verses.13:2: And Saul chose for himself three thousand men from the men of Israel; and two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in Mount Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Geba of Benjamin; and the rest of the people he sent away, each to his own tent.
verses.13:3: And Jonathan struck down Nasib the foreigner who was on the hill, and the foreigners heard of it. And Saul sounded the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, "The slaves have rebelled!"
verses.13:4: And all Israel heard people saying, "Saul has struck down Nasib the foreigner," and Israel was put to shame among the foreigners; and the sons of Israel went up after Saul at Gilgal.
verses.13:5: And the foreigners assembled for war against Israel, and there came up against Israel thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people like the sand beside the sea in multitude; and they came up and encamped in Michmash, opposite Beth Horon to the rear.
verses.13:6: And the men of Israel saw that they were in distress, so that they could not advance; and the people hid themselves in the caves, and in the enclosures, and in the rocks, and in the pits, and in the cisterns.
verses.13:7: And those who crossed over crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was still in Gilgal, and all the people were dismayed behind him.
verses.13:8: And he waited seven days according to the testimony, as Samuel had said; yet Samuel did not arrive at Gilgal, and his people were scattered from him.
verses.13:9: And Saul said, "Draw near, that I may offer a burnt offering and peace offerings." And he offered up the burnt offering.
verses.13:10: And it came to pass, as he finished offering up the burnt offering, that Samuel arrived; and Saul went out to meet him, to bless him.
verses.13:11: And Samuel said, "What have you done?" And Saul said, "Because I saw how the people were scattered from me, and you did not arrive as you had appointed in the testimony of the days, and the foreigners were gathered together at Michmash,
verses.13:12: and I said, 'Now the foreigners will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not implored the face of the Lord.' So I compelled myself and offered up the burnt offering."
verses.13:13: And Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly, because you have not kept my commandment which the Lord commanded you; for now the Lord would have established your kingdom forever over Israel.
verses.13:14: And now your kingdom shall not stand; and the Lord will seek for Himself a man after His own heart, and the Lord will appoint him as ruler over His people, because you have not kept what the Lord commanded you."
verses.13:15: And Samuel arose and departed from Gilgal on his way; and the remnant of the people went up after Saul to meet the men of war. When they arrived from Gilgal at Gibeah of Benjamin, Saul numbered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.
verses.13:16: And Saul and Jonathan his son, and the people and those who were found with them, sat in Geba of Benjamin and wept; and the foreigners had encamped in Michmash.
verses.13:17: And a destroyer went out from the field of the foreigners in three companies: one company facing the way of Ophrah toward Shual,
verses.13:18: and one company facing the way of Beth Horon, and one company facing the way of Geba that overlooks Gai of Samein.
verses.13:19: And no craftsman in iron was found in all the land of Israel, for the foreigners said, "Lest the Hebrews make a sword and a spear."
verses.13:20: And all Israel went down to the land of the foreigners to forge each man his scythe and tool, and each man his ax and his sickle.
verses.13:21: And the vintage was ready for harvesting; and the tools were three shekels for a tooth, and for the ax and for the sickle the standing rate was the same.
verses.13:22: And it came to pass in the days of the battle of Michmash, that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and with Jonathan; yet they were found with Saul and with Jonathan his son.
verses.13:23: And some from the garrison of the foreigners went out to the crossing of Michmash; and he did not tell his father.
verses.14:1: And a day came when Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor, "Come, and let us cross over to Messab of the Philistines, which is on that other side." But he did not tell his father.
verses.14:2: Now Saul was sitting at the edge of the hill beneath the pomegranate tree that was in Magon, and there were with him about six hundred men.
verses.14:3: And Ahijah the son of Ahitub, brother of Jochabel, the son of Phinehas, the son of Levi, was priest of God in Shiloh, bearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had departed.
verses.14:4: Now in the midst of the pass by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the outpost of the Philistines, there was a crag of rock on this side and a crag of rock on that side, and a tooth of rock on this side; the name of the one was Bazes, and the name of the other was Sennaar.
verses.14:5: The one way was from the north as one comes to Michmash, and the other way was from the south as one comes to Geba.
verses.14:6: Then Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, "Come, let us cross over to Messaph of these uncircumcised men; perhaps the Lord will act for us, for there is nothing to restrain the Lord from saving by many or by few."
verses.14:7: And the one who bore his armor said to him, "Do all toward which your heart inclines; behold, I am with you—as your heart is, so is my heart."
verses.14:8: Then Jonathan said, "Behold, we are crossing over to the men, and we will roll down toward them.
verses.14:9: If they say thus to us, 'Stand back there until we send word to you,' then we will stand in our own place and will by no means go up against them.
verses.14:10: And if they say thus to us, 'Come up to us,' then we will go up, for the Lord has delivered them into our hands; this is the sign to us."
verses.14:11: So both of them entered into Messaph of the Philistines. And the Philistines said, "Behold, the Hebrews are coming out of their holes where they hid themselves."
verses.14:12: And the men of Messaph answered Jonathan and the one who bore his armor and said, "Come up to us, and we will make a matter known to you." Then Jonathan said to the one who bore his armor, "Come up after me, for the Lord has delivered them into the hands of Israel."
verses.14:13: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and on his feet, and the one who bore his armor with him. And they looked upon the face of Jonathan, and he struck them down, and the one who bore his armor was dealing further blows behind him.
verses.14:14: And that first slaughter which Jonathan and the one who bore his armor struck down was about twenty men, with darts and pebbles of the field.
verses.14:15: And there came a terror in the camp and in the field, and all the people—those in Messaph and the destroyers—were seized with terror, and they would not act; and the earth was dismayed, and there came a terror from the Lord.
verses.14:16: Now the watchmen of Saul in Geba of Benjamin looked, and behold, the camp was thrown into confusion on this side and on that.
verses.14:17: Then Saul said to the people who were with him, "Make a count now, and see who has departed from among you." And they made a count, and behold, Jonathan and the one who bore his armor were not found.
verses.14:18: And Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring near the ephod." For he bore the ephod on that day before Israel.
verses.14:19: And it came to pass, while Saul was speaking to the priest, that the uproar in the camp of the Philistines kept increasing more and more. So Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hands."
verses.14:20: Then Saul and all the people who were with him went up, and they came to the battle; and behold, every man's sword was against his neighbor, a very great confusion.
verses.14:21: Moreover, the servants who were with the Philistines yesterday and the day before, who had gone up into the camp, they also turned back to be with Israel, with those who were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.14:22: And all Israel who were hiding in Mount Ephraim also heard that the Philistines had fled, and they too joined in pursuit after them into the battle.
verses.14:23: So the Lord saved Israel on that day. And the battle passed beyond Bamoth, and all the people who were with Saul were about ten thousand men; and the battle was spread to every city in Mount Ephraim.
verses.14:24: And Saul committed a great error of ignorance on that day, and he laid a curse upon the people, saying, "Cursed is the man who eats bread until evening, and I shall take vengeance on my enemy." So none of the people tasted bread.
verses.14:25: Yet all the land was taking its meal. Now Jaal was a forest of a beehive upon the face of the field.
verses.14:26: And the people entered the beehive, and behold, they went on speaking; and behold, there was no one returning his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath of the Lord.
verses.14:27: But Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under an oath; therefore he stretched out the tip of his staff that was in his hand and dipped it into the honeycomb, and returned his hand to his mouth, and his eyes saw clearly.
verses.14:28: Then one of the people answered and said, "Your father solemnly bound the people with an oath, saying, 'Cursed is the man who eats bread today.'" And the people grew faint.
verses.14:29: And Jonathan understood and said, "My father has undone the land! See how my eyes saw clearly because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.14:30: How much more if the people had indeed eaten today of the spoil of their enemies which they found! For now the slaughter among the Philistines would have been greater."
verses.14:31: And on that day he struck down some of the Philistines in Michmash; and the people became exceedingly weary.
verses.14:32: Then the people turned aside to the spoil, and the people took flocks and herds and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people ate them with the blood.
verses.14:33: And it was told to Saul, saying, "The people have sinned against the Lord by eating with the blood." Then Saul said, "In Getthaim, roll a great stone to me here."
verses.14:34: And Saul said, "Disperse yourselves among the people, and tell them to bring here each man his calf and each man his own sheep, and let him slaughter it upon this, and you shall by no means sin against the Lord by eating with the blood." So all the people brought, each man what was in his hand, and they slaughtered them there.
verses.14:35: And Saul built an altar there to the Lord; in this Saul began to build an altar to the Lord.
verses.14:36: Then Saul said, "Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and let us plunder among them until day dawns, and let us not leave a man among them." And they said, "Do all that is good in your sight." But the priest said, "Let us draw near here to God."
verses.14:37: So Saul inquired of God, "Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You deliver them into the hands of Israel?" But He did not answer him on that day.
verses.14:38: Then Saul said, "Bring near here all the cornerstones of Israel, and know and see in whom this sin has occurred today;
verses.14:39: for as the Lord lives, who saved Israel, even if the answer is against Jonathan my son, he shall surely die." And there was no one who answered from among all the people.
verses.14:40: Then he said to all Israel, "You shall be for servitude, and I and Jonathan my son shall be for servitude." And the people said to Saul, "Do what is good in your sight."
verses.14:41: And Saul said, "O Lord God of Israel, why have You not answered Your servant today? Is the iniquity in me or in Jonathan my son? O Lord God of Israel, give clear signs; and if it says thus, give now to Your people Israel, give now holiness." And Jonathan and Saul were taken by lot, and the people went out.
verses.14:42: Then Saul said, "Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son; whomever the Lord chooses by lot, let him die." And the people said to Saul, "This thing is not to be!" Yet Saul prevailed over the people, and they cast lots between him and Jonathan his son, and Jonathan was taken by lot.
verses.14:43: Then Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." And Jonathan told him and said, "I certainly tasted a little honey with the tip of the staff that was in my hand; behold, I must die."
verses.14:44: And Saul said to him, "May God do so to me, and more also, for you shall surely die today."
verses.14:45: Then the people said to Saul, "Shall he be put to death today who has accomplished this great salvation in Israel? As the Lord lives, not a hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for the people of God have brought about this day." So the people prayed for Jonathan on that day, and he did not die.
verses.14:46: Then Saul went up from pursuing after the Philistines, and the Philistines departed to their own place.
verses.14:47: And Saul obtained by lot to reign—he was allotted the work over Israel—and he fought on every side against all his enemies: against Moab, and against the sons of Ammon, and against the sons of Edom, and against Baitheor, and against the king of Zobah, and against the Philistines; wherever he turned, he was saved.
verses.14:48: And he gathered a force of Aunanein, and struck down Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of those who trampled him.
verses.14:49: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Jessiul, and Malchishua. And the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the second was Michal.
verses.14:50: And the name of his wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahinaas. And the name of the commander of the army was Abner, the son of Neri, the son of a kinsman of Saul.
verses.14:51: And Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Jamin, the son of Abier.
verses.14:52: And the war against the Philistines was fierce all the days of Saul; and when Saul saw every mighty man and every man who was a son of strength, he gathered them to himself.
verses.15:1: And Samuel said to Saul, "The Lord sent me to anoint you as king over Israel; and now, listen to the voice of the Lord.
verses.15:2: Thus says the Lord of hosts: 'Now I will avenge what Amalek did to Israel, how he met him on the way as he came up out of Egypt.
verses.15:3: And now go, and you shall strike Amalek and Jerim and all that belongs to him, and you shall not preserve anything of his, but shall utterly destroy him; and you shall devote him and all that belongs to him to destruction, and you shall not spare him, but shall slay from man even to woman, from infant to nursing child, from calf to sheep, and from camel to donkey.'"
verses.15:4: And Saul summoned the people and mustered them in Gilgal: four hundred thousand troops, and of Judah thirty thousand troops.
verses.15:5: And Saul came as far as the cities of Amalek, and laid an ambush in the torrent valley.
verses.15:6: And Saul said to the Kenite, "Depart and turn aside from the midst of the Amalekite, lest I add you with him; for you showed mercy to the sons of Israel when they came up out of Egypt." And the Kenite turned aside from the midst of Amalek.
verses.15:7: And Saul struck Amalek from Havilah all the way to Asshur, which is before the face of Egypt.
verses.15:8: And he captured Agag king of Amalek alive, and he slew all the people of Jerim with the edge of the sword.
verses.15:9: And Saul and all the people preserved Agag alive, and the best of the flocks and of the herds, and of the provisions and of the vineyards, and of all that was good, and he was unwilling to utterly destroy them; but everything that was dishonored and despised they utterly destroyed.
verses.15:10: Then the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying,
verses.15:11: "I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned back from following Me and has not kept My words." And Samuel was disheartened, and he cried out to the Lord all the night.
verses.15:12: And Samuel rose early and went to meet Israel in the morning. And it was reported to Saul, saying, "Samuel has come to Carmel, and he has set up a monument for himself." And he turned the chariot around and went down to Gilgal to Saul; and behold, he was offering up a burnt offering to the Lord, the choicest of the spoils which he had brought from Amalek.
verses.15:13: And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you of the Lord! I have fulfilled all that the Lord spoke."
verses.15:14: And Samuel said, "What then is this sound of the flock in my ears, and the sound of the cattle which I hear?"
verses.15:15: And Saul said, "From Amalek I have brought them, which the people spared—the choicest of the flock and of the cattle—in order that they might be sacrificed to the Lord your God; and the rest I have utterly destroyed."
verses.15:16: And Samuel said to Saul, "Be quiet, and I will declare to you what the Lord spoke to me this night." And he said to him, "Speak."
verses.15:17: And Samuel said to Saul, "Are you not small before Him, a leader of the scepter of a tribe of Israel? Yet the Lord anointed you as king over Israel.
verses.15:18: And the Lord sent you on a way and said to you, 'Go and utterly destroy; you shall slay those who sin against Me, even Amalek, and fight against them until you make an end of them.'
verses.15:19: Why then did you not obey the voice of the Lord, but rushed to seize upon the spoils and did what was evil in the sight of the Lord?"
verses.15:20: And Saul said to Samuel, "Because I listened to the voice of the people! Yet I walked in the way on which the Lord sent me, and brought Agag king of Amalek, and utterly destroyed Amalek.
verses.15:21: And the people took from the spoils flocks and herds, the choicest of the things devoted to destruction, before the Lord our God in Gilgal."
verses.15:22: And Samuel said, "Are burnt offerings and sacrifices as desirable to the Lord as obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, obedience is above a good sacrifice, and giving heed is above the fat of rams.
verses.15:23: For sin is divination, and grief and toil bring on healing. Because you have rejected the word of the Lord, the Lord will also reject you, so that you shall not be king over Israel."
verses.15:24: And Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have transgressed the word of the Lord and your saying, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
verses.15:25: Now therefore, please take away my sin, and return with me, that I may worship the Lord your God."
verses.15:26: And Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord will reject you so that you shall not be king over Israel."
verses.15:27: And Samuel turned his face to depart, and Saul laid hold of the hem of his mantle and tore it.
verses.15:28: And Samuel said to him, "The Lord has torn your kingdom from Israel out of your hand today, and He will give it to your neighbor who is better than you.
verses.15:29: And Israel shall be divided in two, and He will not turn back nor relent; for He is not as a man, that He should relent."
verses.15:30: And Saul said, "I have sinned; yet please honor me before the elders of Israel and before my people, and return with me, and I will worship the Lord your God."
verses.15:31: So Samuel turned back after Saul, and he worshiped the Lord.
verses.15:32: And Samuel said, "Bring Agag king of Amalek to me." And Agag came to him trembling. And Agag said, "Is death indeed so bitter?"
verses.15:33: And Samuel said to Agag, "Just as your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be made childless among women." And Samuel slaughtered Agag before the Lord in Gilgal.
verses.15:34: Then Samuel departed to Armathaim, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah.
verses.15:35: And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul; and the Lord regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.16:1: And the Lord said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn over Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and come, I will send you to Jesse even to Bethlehem; for I have seen among his sons one to reign for Me."
verses.16:2: And Samuel said, "How can I go? For Saul will hear and slay me." And the Lord said, "Take a heifer from the herd in your hand, and you shall say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the Lord.'
verses.16:3: And you shall invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do; and you shall anoint him whom I tell you."
verses.16:4: And Samuel did all that the Lord had spoken to him, and he came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city were alarmed at meeting him, and they said, "Is your coming in peace, O seer?"
verses.16:5: And he said, "In peace; I have come to sacrifice to the Lord. Sanctify yourselves and rejoice with me today." And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and invited them to the sacrifice.
verses.16:6: And it came to pass as they entered that he saw Eliab, and he said, "Surely His anointed is before the Lord."
verses.16:7: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Do not look upon his appearance nor upon the stature of his height, for I have rejected him; for God does not see as a man beholds, because man looks upon the face, but God looks upon the heart."
verses.16:8: And Jesse called Amminadab, and he passed before Samuel; and he said, "Neither has God chosen this one."
verses.16:9: And Jesse brought Shammah forward; and he said, "Neither has the Lord chosen this one."
verses.16:10: Thus Jesse brought his seven sons before Samuel; and Samuel said, "The Lord has not chosen among these."
verses.16:11: And Samuel said to Jesse, "Are there no more of the young men?" And he said, "There is still the youngest; behold, he is tending the flock." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and bring him, for we will by no means recline at table until he comes."
verses.16:12: So he sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes, and good in appearance to the Lord. And the Lord said to Samuel, "Arise and anoint David, for this one is good."
verses.16:13: And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon David from that day onward. Then Samuel arose and departed to Armathaim.
verses.16:14: Now the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord choked him.
verses.16:15: And the servants of Saul said to him, "Behold now, an evil spirit of the Lord is choking you.
verses.16:16: Let your servants now speak before you, and let them seek out for our lord a man who knows how to play upon the lyre; and it shall be, whenever an evil spirit is upon you, that he will play upon his lyre, and it shall be well with you, and it will give you rest."
verses.16:17: And Saul said to his servants, "Provide for me now a man who plays skillfully, and bring him in to me."
verses.16:18: Then one of his young men answered and said, "Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play music; and the man is prudent, and a warrior, and wise in speech, and a man of handsome appearance, and the Lord is with him."
verses.16:19: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, "Send to me your son David, who is with your flock."
verses.16:20: And Jesse took a homer of bread, and a skin of wine, and one kid of the goats, and sent them by the hand of his son David to Saul.
verses.16:21: And David came in to Saul and stood before him; and he loved him exceedingly, and he became his armor-bearer.
verses.16:22: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my sight."
verses.16:23: And it came to pass, whenever an evil spirit was upon Saul, that David would take the lyre and play with his hand; and Saul would be refreshed and it was well with him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
verses.17:1: Now the Philistines gathered their armies for war, and assembled at Socoh of Idumea, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephermem.
verses.17:2: And Saul and the men of Israel assembled and encamped in the valley; they drew up in battle array opposite the Philistines.
verses.17:3: And the Philistines stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, with a circle between them.
verses.17:4: And a mighty man came out from the ranks of the Philistines, whose name was Goliath, from Gath; his height was four cubits and a span.
verses.17:5: And a helmet was upon his head, and he was clothed with a coat of chain mail, and the weight of his coat of mail was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron;
verses.17:6: and bronze greaves were upon his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders;
verses.17:7: and the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam, and his spearhead was six hundred shekels of iron; and the one who carried his armor went before him.
verses.17:8: And he stood up and shouted to the ranks of Israel, and said to them, "Why do you come out to draw up in battle array opposite us? Am I not a Philistine, and you Hebrews and Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
verses.17:9: And if he is able to fight against me, and if he strikes me down, then we shall be your servants; but if I prevail and strike him down, you shall be our servants and serve us."
verses.17:10: And the Philistine said, "Behold, I have reproached the ranks of Israel today, on this very day; give me a man, and we shall both fight in single combat."
verses.17:11: And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and exceedingly afraid.
verses.17:32: Then David said to Saul, "Do not let the heart of my lord fail because of him; your servant will go and fight with this Philistine."
verses.17:33: And Saul said to David, "You are not able to go against the Philistine to fight with him, for you are a lad, and he is a man of war from his youth."
verses.17:34: And David said to Saul, "Your servant was shepherding for his father in the flock; and whenever the lion and the bear came and took a sheep from the herd,
verses.17:35: I went out after it and struck it, and snatched the sheep from its mouth; and if it rose up against me, I seized it by its throat, and struck it and put it to death.
verses.17:36: Your servant has struck both the bear and the lion, and the uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them. Shall I not go and strike him down, and take away reproach from Israel today? For who is this uncircumcised one, who has reproached the ranks of the living God?
verses.17:37: The Lord, who delivered me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, He will deliver me from the hand of this uncircumcised Philistine." And Saul said to David, "Go, and the Lord shall be with you."
verses.17:38: And Saul clothed David with a mantle, and put a bronze helmet about his head,
verses.17:39: and girded David with his sword over his mantle; and he grew weary after walking once and twice. And David said to Saul, "I cannot walk in these, for I have not tested them." So they removed them from him.
verses.17:40: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five perfect stones from the brook, and put them in the shepherd's pouch that he had for gathering, with his sling in his hand; and he drew near to the Philistine man.
verses.17:42: And Goliath saw David and disdained him, for he was a lad, and he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes.
verses.17:43: And the Philistine said to David, "Am I like a dog, that you come against me with a staff and stones?" And David said, "No, but worse than a dog." And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.17:44: And the Philistine said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of heaven and to the beasts of the earth."
verses.17:45: Then David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield; but I come to you in the name of the Lord God of Sabaoth, of the ranks of Israel, which you have reproached today.
verses.17:46: And today the Lord will deliver you up into my hand, and I will slay you and take your head from you, and I will give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the Philistines on this day to the birds of heaven and to the wild beasts of the earth; and all the earth shall know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.17:47: And all this assembly shall know that the Lord does not save with sword and spear; for the battle belongs to the Lord, and the Lord will deliver you into our hands."
verses.17:48: And the Philistine arose and went to meet David.
verses.17:49: And David reached out his hand into the pouch and took one stone from there, and slung it and struck the Philistine upon his forehead; and the stone passed through the helmet into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the ground.
verses.17:51: Then David ran and stood over him, and took his sword and put him to death, and cut off his head. And the Philistines saw that their mighty man was dead, and they fled.
verses.17:52: And the men of Israel and Judah arose and raised a war cry, and pursued after them as far as the entrance of Gath and as far as the gate of Ashkelon; and the wounded of the Philistines fell along the road of the gates, even to Gath and to Ekron.
verses.17:53: And the men of Israel returned, turning back from pursuing the Philistines, and they trampled their camps.
verses.17:54: And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put his armor in his tent.
verses.18:6: And the dancing women came out from all the cities of Israel to meet David, with timbrels, with gladness, and with cymbals.
verses.18:7: And the women led the song and said, "Saul has struck down in his thousands, and David in his ten thousands."
