verses.18:8: And the matter appeared evil in the eyes of Saul concerning this saying, and he said, "To David they have given the ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands."
verses.18:9: And Saul eyed David with suspicion from that day and onward.
verses.18:12: And Saul was afraid before the face of David,
verses.18:13: and he removed him from himself and appointed him for himself as a commander of a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.
verses.18:14: And David acted with understanding in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.
verses.18:15: And Saul saw that he acted with great understanding, and he stood in dread before his face.
verses.18:16: And all Israel and Judah loved David, because he came in and went out before the face of the people.
verses.18:20: Now Michal the daughter of Saul loved David; and it was reported to Saul, and it was right in his eyes.
verses.18:21: And Saul said, "I will give her to him, and she shall be a stumbling block to him." And the hand of the Philistines was upon Saul.
verses.18:22: And Saul commanded his servants, saying, "Speak secretly to David, saying, 'Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you; now therefore become son-in-law to the king.'"
verses.18:23: And the servants of Saul spoke these words in the ears of David. And David said, "Is it a light thing in your eyes to become son-in-law to a king? And I am a lowly man and not held in honor."
verses.18:24: And the servants of Saul reported to him according to these words that David had spoken.
verses.18:25: And Saul said, "Thus you shall say to David, 'The king does not desire any dowry, except one hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to take vengeance on the enemies of the king.'" Now Saul planned to cast him into the hands of the Philistines.
verses.18:26: And the servants of Saul reported these words to David, and the word was right in the eyes of David to become son-in-law to the king.
verses.18:27: And David arose and went, he and his men, and struck down among the Philistines one hundred men; and he brought up their foreskins to the king, and became son-in-law to the king, and he gave him his daughter Michal as his wife.
verses.18:28: And Saul saw that the Lord was with David, and that all Israel loved him,
verses.18:29: and he stood in dread of David yet more.
verses.19:1: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, to put David to death.
verses.19:2: Now Jonathan, the son of Saul, delighted exceedingly in David; and Jonathan told David, saying, "Saul seeks to put you to death. Therefore be on your guard tomorrow morning, and hide yourself and sit in secret.
verses.19:3: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak concerning you to my father; and I will see whatever may be, and I will tell you."
verses.19:4: And Jonathan spoke good things concerning David to Saul his father, and said to him, "Do not let the king sin against your servant David, because he has not sinned against you, and his deeds are exceedingly good.
verses.19:5: And he put his life in his hand and struck down the foreigner, and the Lord wrought a great deliverance, and all Israel saw and rejoiced. Why then do you sin against innocent blood, to put David to death without cause?"
verses.19:6: And Saul heeded the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, saying, "As the Lord lives, he shall not die."
verses.19:7: So Jonathan called David and told him all these words. And Jonathan brought David in to Saul, and he was before him as yesterday and the day before.
verses.19:8: And war came again against David; and David prevailed and fought against the foreigners, and struck them with an exceedingly great blow, and they fled from before his face.
verses.19:9: And an evil spirit of God came upon Saul while he was sleeping in the house, and a spear was in his hand, and David was playing music with his hands.
verses.19:10: And Saul sought to strike the spear into David, but David turned aside from the presence of Saul; and he drove the spear into the wall, and David withdrew and escaped safely.
verses.19:11: And it came to pass in that night that Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him, in order to put him to death in the morning. And Michal his wife told David, saying, "If you do not save your own life tonight, tomorrow you shall be put to death."
verses.19:12: So Michal let David down through the window, and he went away and fled and escaped safely.
verses.19:13: And Michal took the cenotaphs and laid them upon the bed, and she placed a liver of goats at its head, and covered them with a garment.
verses.19:14: And Saul sent messengers to take David, and they said that he was ill.
verses.19:15: And he sent for David, saying, "Bring him on the bed to me, to put him to death."
verses.19:16: And the messengers came, and behold, the cenotaphs were upon the bed, and a liver of goats was at its head.
verses.19:17: And Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me in this way, and sent away my enemy so that he escaped safely?" And Michal said to Saul, "He himself said, 'Send me away; otherwise, I will put you to death.'"
verses.19:18: So David fled and escaped safely, and he came to Samuel in Ramathaim and told him all that Saul had done to him. And David and Samuel went and dwelt in Auath in Ramah.
verses.19:19: And it was reported to Saul, saying, "Behold, David is in Auath in Ramah."
verses.19:20: And Saul sent messengers to take David; and they saw the assembly of the prophets, and Samuel was standing, appointed over them. And the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they prophesied.
verses.19:21: And it was reported to Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul again sent a third company of messengers, and they also prophesied.
verses.19:22: Then Saul was furious with wrath, and he himself also went to Ramathaim; and he came as far as the well of the threshing floor that is in Sephei, and he inquired and said, "Where are Samuel and David?" And one said, "Behold, they are in Auath in Ramah."
verses.19:23: So he went from there to Auath in Ramah, and the Spirit of God came upon him also; and he went along prophesying until he came to Auath in Ramah.
verses.19:24: And he stripped off his garments and prophesied before them, and he fell down naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they said, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.20:1: Then David fled from Auath in Ramah, and came before Jonathan and said, "What have I done, and what is my iniquity, and how have I sinned before your father, that he seeks my life?"
verses.20:2: And Jonathan said to him, "Far be it from you! You shall by no means die. Behold, my father will by no means do a small thing and not uncover my ear; and why should my father conceal this matter? This is not so."
verses.20:3: And David answered Jonathan and said, "Your father surely knows that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said that Jonathan must not know this, lest he be unwilling. But as the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, as he has said, the space between me and death is filled up."
verses.20:4: And Jonathan said to David, "What does your soul desire, and what shall I do for you?"
verses.20:5: And David said to Jonathan, "Behold now, tomorrow is the new moon, and I will surely not sit down to eat; so you shall send me away, and I will hide myself in the plain until evening.
verses.20:6: If your father indeed misses me, then you shall say, 'David earnestly asked leave of me to run to Bethlehem his city, because a sacrifice of the days is there for the whole tribe.'
verses.20:7: If he says thus, 'It is well,' then there is peace for your servant; but if he answers you harshly, know that evil is fully determined by him.
verses.20:8: And you shall show mercy to your servant, because you have brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with yourself. Yet if there is iniquity in your servant, put me to death yourself; for why should you thus bring me to your father?"
verses.20:9: And Jonathan said, "Far be it from you! For if I surely know that evil is determined by my father to come upon you, even if it is not against your cities, I will tell you."
verses.20:10: Then David said to Jonathan, "Who will tell me if your father answers harshly?"
verses.20:11: And Jonathan said to David, "Go and remain in the field." So both of them went out into the field.
verses.20:12: Then Jonathan said to David, "The Lord God of Israel knows that I will sound out my father about this time on the third day; and behold, if there is good concerning David, and I do not send to you in the field,
verses.20:13: may God do so to Jonathan, and more also! For I will report the evil against you and uncover your ear, and I will send you away, and you shall depart in peace; and the Lord shall be with you, just as He was with my father.
verses.20:14: And while I am still living, you shall indeed show mercy to me; and if I surely die,
verses.20:15: you shall not cut off your mercy from my house forever; and if not, when the Lord cuts off the enemies of David, every one from the face of the earth,
verses.20:16: may the name of Jonathan be found out from the house of David; and may the Lord seek out the enemies of David."
verses.20:17: And Jonathan swore yet again to David, because he loved the soul of the one who loved him.
verses.20:18: And Jonathan said, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be missed.
verses.20:19: And you shall stay three days and watch carefully, and you shall come to your place where you hid yourself on the workday, and you shall sit beside that Ergab.
verses.20:20: And I will shoot three times with arrows, sending them forth toward Harmattarei.
verses.20:21: And behold, I will send the lad, saying, 'Come, find the arrow for me.' If I expressly say to the lad, 'Here is the arrow on this side of you; take it,' then come; for there is peace for you, and there is no word of the Lord, as the Lord lives.
verses.20:22: But if I say thus to the young man, 'Here is the arrow beyond you,' then go, for the Lord has sent you away.
verses.20:23: And as for the word which you and I have spoken, behold, the Lord is witness between me and you forever."
verses.20:24: So David hid himself in the field. And the new moon came, and the king came to the table to eat.
verses.20:25: And he sat upon his seat, as once and again, upon the seat by the wall; and he came before Jonathan, and Abner sat at Saul's side, and David's place was missed.
verses.20:26: Yet Saul spoke nothing on that day, for he said, "It appears to be an occurrence—he is not clean, because he has not been purified."
verses.20:27: And it came to pass on the day after the new moon, on the second day, that David's place was missed. And Saul said to Jonathan his son, "Why has the son of Jesse not come to the table, both yesterday and today?"
verses.20:28: And Jonathan answered Saul and said to him, "David asked leave of me to go as far as Bethlehem his city,
verses.20:29: and he said, 'Send me away now, for we have a sacrifice of the tribe in the city, and my brethren have commanded me. And now, if I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away now and see my brethren.' Therefore he has not come to the king's table."
verses.20:30: Then Saul was exceedingly furious with wrath against Jonathan, and he said to him, "Son of deserting maidens, do I not know that you are a partner with the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of the uncovering of your mother?
verses.20:31: For all the days that the son of Jesse lives upon the earth, your kingdom shall not be established. Now therefore send and take the young man, for he is a son of death."
verses.20:32: And Jonathan answered Saul, "Why should he die? What has he done?"
verses.20:33: And Saul lifted up the spear against Jonathan to put him to death; and Jonathan knew that this evil was fully determined by his father, to put David to death.
verses.20:34: So Jonathan sprang up from the table in fierce wrath, and he ate no bread on the second day of the month, because his father had fully resolved against him.
verses.20:35: And it came to pass in the morning that Jonathan went out into the field, just as he had appointed for the testimony of David, and a little lad was with him.
verses.20:36: And he said to the lad, "Run, find for me the arrows which I shoot." And the lad ran, and he shot the arrow and sent it beyond.
verses.20:37: And the lad came to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot; and Jonathan cried out behind the young man and said, "There is the arrow beyond you!"
verses.20:38: And Jonathan cried out behind his lad, saying, "Make haste quickly, and do not stand still!" And Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows to his master.
verses.20:39: And the lad knew nothing, except Jonathan and David.
verses.20:40: And Jonathan gave his weapons to his lad, and said to his lad, "Go, enter into the city."
verses.20:41: And as the lad entered, David arose from the Argab and fell upon his face and bowed down to him three times; and each kissed his companion, and each wept with his companion to a great extremity.
verses.20:42: And Jonathan said, "Go in peace, and as we both have sworn in the name of the Lord, saying, 'The Lord shall be witness between me and you, and between your seed forever.'"
verses.21:1: And David arose and departed, and Jonathan went into the city.
verses.21:2: And David came to Nob, to Abimelech the priest; and Abimelech was alarmed at meeting him, and said to him, "Why is it that you are alone, and no one is with you?"
verses.21:3: And David said to the priest, "The king has commanded me a matter today, and said to me, 'Let no one know the matter concerning which I am sending you, and about which I have commanded you.' And I have solemnly instructed the young men at the place called Faithfulness of God, Phellani Maemoni.
verses.21:4: And now, are there five loaves of bread under your hand? Give into my hand whatever is found."
verses.21:5: And the priest answered David and said, "There are no common loaves under my hand, but only holy loaves; if the young men have kept themselves from women, then they shall eat."
verses.21:6: And David answered the priest and said to him, "Indeed, we have abstained from women since yesterday and the third day; when I went out on the journey, all the young men were purified. And is the journey itself common? For it shall be sanctified today because of my vessels."
verses.21:7: So Abimelech the priest gave him the loaves of the presentation; for there were no loaves there except the loaves of the Presence, which had been taken away from the presence of the Lord so that warm bread might be set out on the day he took them.
verses.21:8: Now one of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained—Neessaran—before the Lord; and his name was Doeg the Syrian, tending the mules of Saul.
verses.21:9: And David said to Abimelech, "See if there is here under your hand a spear or a sword; for I have not taken my sword and weapons in my hand, because the king's matter was urgent."
verses.21:10: And the priest said, "Behold, the sword of Goliath the foreigner, whom you struck down in the valley of Elah—and it was wrapped in a garment. If you will take this one, take it for yourself, for there is no other besides this one here." And David said, "Behold, there is none like it; give it to me."
verses.21:11: And he gave it to him. Then David arose and fled on that day from the presence of Saul; and David came to Achish, king of Gath.
verses.21:12: And the servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Was it not for this man that the dancing women led the song, saying, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
verses.21:13: And David laid the words in his heart, and was exceedingly afraid before Achish, king of Gath.
verses.21:14: So he altered his countenance before him and pretended on that day; and he drummed upon the doors of the city, and staggered about in his hands, and fell against the doors of the gate, and his saliva ran down upon his beard.
verses.21:15: Then Achish said to his servants, "Behold, you see a man seized with madness! Why have you brought him in to me?
verses.21:16: Do I lack madmen, that you have brought him in to act madly before me? This man shall not enter into the house."
verses.22:1: So David departed from there and escaped safely, and came to the cave of Adullam; and his brethren and the house of his father heard of it, and they went down to him there.
verses.22:2: And everyone who was in distress, and everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was deeply grieved in soul gathered to him; and he became a leader over them. And there were with him about four hundred men.
verses.22:3: Then David departed from there to Mizpah of Moab; and he said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother stay with you, until I know what God will do for me."
verses.22:4: And he pleaded before the face of the king of Moab, and they dwelt with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.
verses.22:5: Now Gad the prophet said to David, "Do not dwell in the stronghold; depart, and you shall come into the land of Judah." So David departed, and came and dwelt in the city of Sarik.
verses.22:6: And Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered. Now Saul was sitting on the hill below the field that is in Bamah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing beside him.
verses.22:7: And Saul spoke to his servants who were standing beside him, and said to them, "Hear now, O sons of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse truly give all of you fields and vineyards, and appoint all of you captains of hundreds and captains of thousands?
verses.22:8: For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who uncovers my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse; and there is none among you who grieves for me and uncovers my ear, that my son has stirred up my servant against me as an enemy, as it is this day."
verses.22:9: Then Doeg the Syrian, who was set over the mules of Saul, answered and said, "I have seen the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Abimelech the son of Ahitub, the priest;
verses.22:10: and he inquired of God for him, and gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the foreigner."
verses.22:11: So the king sent to summon Abimelech the son of Ahitub, and all the sons of his father, the priests who were in Nob; and all of them came to the king.
verses.22:12: And Saul said, "Hear now, son of Ahitub!" And he said, "Behold, here I am; speak, lord."
verses.22:13: And Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, to set him against me as an enemy, as it is this day?"
verses.22:14: And he answered the king and said, "And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, who is also the king's son-in-law, and commander over all your bidding, and honored in your house?
verses.22:15: Have I only today begun to inquire of God for him? Far be it! May the king not lay any charge against his servant, nor against all the house of his father; for your servant knew nothing of all these things, whether a small matter or a great."
verses.22:16: And King Saul said, "You shall surely die, Abimelech, you and all the house of your father."
verses.22:17: Then the king said to the runners who stood beside him, "Draw near and put to death the priests of the Lord, because their hand is also with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear." Yet the servants of the king would not lift their hands to sin against the priests of the Lord.
verses.22:18: And the king said to Doeg, "Turn and fall upon the priests." So Doeg the Syrian turned and put to death the priests of the Lord on that day, three hundred and five men, all bearing an ephod.
verses.22:19: And he struck Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, from man to woman, from infant to nursing child, and calf and donkey and sheep.
verses.22:20: Now one son of Abimelech the son of Ahitub escaped safely, and his name was Abiathar; and he fled after David.
verses.22:21: And Abiathar reported to David that Saul had put to death all the priests of the Lord.
verses.22:22: And David said to Abiathar, "I knew on that day that Doeg the Syrian would surely report it to Saul; I am responsible for the lives of the house of your father.
verses.22:23: Remain with me; do not be afraid; for wherever I seek a place for my own life, I will seek one for your life also, for you are safeguarded with me."
verses.23:1: And it was reported to David, saying, "Behold, the foreigners are fighting in Keilah, and they are plundering; they are trampling the threshing floors."
verses.23:2: Therefore David inquired through the Lord, saying, "Shall I go and strike down these foreigners?" And the Lord said, "Go, and you shall strike among these foreigners, and you shall strike Keilah."
verses.23:3: And David's men said to him, "Behold, we are afraid here in Judea; and how will it be if we go to Keilah? Shall we enter into the spoils of the foreigners?"
verses.23:4: Then David inquired once more through the Lord. And the Lord answered him and said to him, "Arise and go down to Keilah, for I am delivering the foreigners into your hands."
verses.23:5: So David and the men who were with him went to Keilah and fought among the foreigners; and they fled from before him, and he drove away their livestock, and struck them with a great slaughter. Thus David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
verses.23:6: Now it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Abimelech fled to David, that he also went down with David to Keilah, having an ephod in his hand.
verses.23:7: And it was reported to Saul that David had come to Keilah; and Saul said, "God has sold him into my hands, for he has shut himself in by entering a city of doors and bars."
verses.23:8: So Saul commanded all the people for war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
verses.23:9: And David knew that Saul was not keeping silent about the evil concerning him; and David said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring near the ephod of the Lord."
verses.23:10: And David said, "O Lord God of Israel, Your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come against Keilah to destroy the city because of me.
verses.23:11: Will it be shut up? And now, will Saul come down as Your servant has heard? O Lord God of Israel, declare it to Your servant." And the Lord said, "It shall be shut up."
verses.23:13: Then David and the men who were with him, about four hundred, arose and went out from Keilah, and went wherever they could go. And it was reported to Saul that David had escaped safely from Keilah, so he refrained from going out.
verses.23:14: And he dwelt in the wilderness in Maserem, in the narrow passes, and remained in the wilderness in the hill country of Ziph, in the parched land. And Saul sought him all the days, yet the Lord did not deliver him into his hands.
verses.23:15: And David saw that Saul had come out to seek David; and David was in the parched mountain, in Kaine of Ziph.
verses.23:16: Then Jonathan, the son of Saul, arose and went to David in Kaine, and strengthened his hands in the Lord.
verses.23:17: And he said to him, "Do not fear, for the hand of Saul my father shall by no means find you. You shall be king over Israel, and I shall be second to you; and Saul my father knows it is so."
verses.23:18: So the two of them made a covenant before the Lord. And David remained in Kaine, while Jonathan departed to his own house.
verses.23:19: Then the Ziphites went up from the parched land to Saul on the hill, saying, "Behold, is David not hidden among us in Nessara, in the narrow passes, in Kaine, on the hill of Hachilah, which is on the right of Jeshimon?
verses.23:20: And now, according to all the desire of the king's soul to come down, let him come down to us; they have shut him up into the hands of the king."
verses.23:21: And Saul said to them, "Blessed are you by the Lord, because you have grieved for me.
verses.23:22: Go now and prepare further, and learn his place where his foot will swiftly be, there where you spoke of, lest he act craftily.
verses.23:23: See therefore and learn, and we shall go with you; and it shall be, if he is in the land, that I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah."
verses.23:24: So the Ziphites arose and went ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, toward the west, on the right of Jeshimon.
verses.23:25: And Saul and his men went to seek him. And they reported it to David, so he went down to the rock that is in the wilderness of Maon. And Saul heard of it, and pursued after David into the wilderness of Maon.
verses.23:26: And Saul and his men went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other side of the mountain. And David was taking cover to get away from the presence of Saul, while Saul and his men encamped against David and his men to seize them.
verses.23:27: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hasten and come, for the foreigners have fallen upon the land!"
verses.23:28: Therefore Saul turned back from pursuing after David, and went to meet the foreigners; because of this, that place was called the Divided Rock.
verses.24:1: And David arose from there and dwelt in the narrow passes of En Gedi.
verses.24:2: Now it came to pass, when Saul returned from following after the foreigners, that it was reported to him, saying, "David is in the wilderness of En Gedi."
verses.24:3: And he took with him three thousand chosen men from all Israel, and went to seek David and his men before Eddaiem.
verses.24:4: And he came to the herds of the flocks that were by the way, and there was a cave there; and Saul went in to prepare himself, while David and his men were sitting in the inner part of the cave.
verses.24:5: Then the men of David said to him, "Behold, this is the day of which the Lord spoke to you, to deliver your enemy into your hands, and you shall do to him as seems good in your eyes." And David arose and secretly cut off the corner of Saul's mantle.
verses.24:6: And it came to pass afterward that David's heart struck him because he had cut off the corner of his mantle.
verses.24:7: And David said to his men, "Far be it from me before the Lord, that I should do this thing to the Lord's anointed, to lay my hand against him, for he is the Lord's anointed."
verses.24:8: So David persuaded his men with words, and did not permit them to rise up and slay Saul. And Saul arose and went down the way.
verses.24:9: And David arose after him out of the cave, and David cried out after Saul, saying, "O lord, O king!" And Saul looked behind him, and David stooped with his face to the earth and bowed down before him.
verses.24:10: And David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of the people who say, 'Behold, David seeks your life'?
verses.24:11: Behold, on this day your eyes have seen how the Lord delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and I was not willing to kill you, and I spared you and said, 'I will not lay my hand against my lord, for he is the Lord's anointed.'
verses.24:12: And behold, the corner of your mantle is in my hand; I have cut off the corner and have not killed you. Know and see today that there is no evil in my hand, nor ungodliness and rebellion, and I have not sinned against you; yet you bind my life to take it.
verses.24:13: May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me of you; yet my hand shall not be against you.
verses.24:14: As the ancient proverb says, 'From the lawless shall come forth transgression'; yet my hand shall not be against you.
verses.24:15: And now, after whom do you go out, O king of Israel? After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog, and after a single flea!
verses.24:16: May the Lord be judge and arbiter between me and you; may the Lord see and judge my cause, and render judgment for me out of your hand."
verses.24:17: And it came to pass, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, "Is this your voice, child David?" And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
verses.24:18: And Saul said to David, "You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with good, whereas I have repaid you with evil.
verses.24:19: And you have declared to me today the good that you have done for me, how the Lord shut me up today into your hands and you did not kill me.
verses.24:20: For if anyone should find his enemy in distress and send him away on a good road, the Lord also will repay him with good, even as you have done today.
verses.24:21: And now, behold, I know that you shall surely reign, and the kingdom of Israel shall be established in your hands.
verses.24:22: Now therefore, swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my seed after me, and that you will not blot out my name from the house of my father."
verses.24:23: So David swore to Saul. And Saul went away to his own place, while David and his men went up to the narrow pass of Messara.
verses.25:1: And Samuel died; and all Israel gathered together and lamented for him, and buried him at his house in Ramathaim. And David arose and went down to the wilderness of Maon.
verses.25:2: Now there was a man in Maon whose flocks were in Carmel; and the man was exceedingly great, and he had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats. And it came to pass that he was shearing his flock in Carmel.
verses.25:3: And the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. And his wife was good in understanding and exceedingly fair in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his practices, and the man was dog-like.
verses.25:4: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal the Carmelite was shearing his flock.
verses.25:5: So David sent ten young men, and said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name with peace,
verses.25:6: and you shall say thus: 'For seasons to come, may you be in health, and may your house and all that is yours be in health.
verses.25:7: And now, behold, I have heard that your shepherds who were with us in the wilderness are now shearing for you; and we did not hinder them, nor did we command anything of them all the days that they were in Carmel.
verses.25:8: Ask your young men, and they will report to you. Therefore let your young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a good day; give now whatever your hand may find to your son David.'"
verses.25:9: So the young men came and spoke these words to Nabal, even all these sayings, in the name of David. And he sprang up.
verses.25:10: And Nabal answered David's servants and said, "Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse? Today servants have multiplied who depart each one from the presence of his master.
verses.25:11: Shall I then take my bread and my wine and my meat which I have slaughtered for those who shear my sheep, and give them to men of whom I do not know where they are from?"
verses.25:12: So David's young men turned back on their way, and returned and came and reported to David according to these words.
verses.25:13: And David said to his men, "Let each man gird on his sword." And about four hundred men went up after David, while the two hundred stayed with the baggage.
verses.25:14: Now one of the young men reported to Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, "Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, and he turned away from them.
verses.25:15: Yet the men were exceedingly good to us; they did not hinder us, nor did they command us all the days that we were with them.
verses.25:16: And while we were in the field, they were like a wall around us both by night and by day, all the days that we were with them tending the flock.
verses.25:17: Now therefore, know and consider what you will do, for evil is determined against our master and against his house; and he is a pestilent son, so that one cannot speak to him."
verses.25:18: Then Abigail made haste and took two hundred loaves of bread, and two vessels of wine, and five prepared sheep, and five ephahs of barley meal, and one omer of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and loaded them on the donkeys.
verses.25:19: And she said to her young men, "Go on before me, and behold, I am coming after you." But she did not report it to her husband.
verses.25:20: And it came to pass, as she was riding on the donkey and going down under the shelter of the mountain, that behold, David and his men were coming down to meet her; and she met them.
verses.25:21: Now David had said, "Surely to an unjust end I have guarded all that belongs to him in the wilderness, and we gave no command to take anything of all that is his, yet he has repaid me evil for good.
verses.25:22: May God do so to David, and more also, if I leave of all that belongs to Nabal until morning even one who urinates against a wall."
verses.25:23: And when Abigail saw David, she hastened and leaped down from the donkey, and fell before David upon her face, and bowed down before him to the earth,
verses.25:24: at his feet, and said, "Upon me, my lord, be my iniquity! Let your maidservant speak now in your ears, and hear the word of your maidservant.
verses.25:25: Do not let my lord set his heart upon this pestilent man, for as his name is, so is he: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your maidservant, did not see your young men whom you sent.
verses.25:26: Now therefore, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, since the Lord has restrained you from coming to innocent blood and from saving yourself by your own hand, now let your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord become like Nabal.
verses.25:27: And now, receive the blessing which your maidservant has brought to my lord, and you shall give it to the young men who attend upon my lord.
verses.25:28: Take away, I pray, the transgression of your maidservant; for the Lord will surely make for my lord a faithful house, because the Lord fights the war of my lord, and evil shall never be found in you.
verses.25:29: And a man shall rise up pursuing you and seeking your life, yet the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord God; and the soul of your enemies you shall sling in the midst of the sling.
verses.25:30: And it shall come to pass, when the Lord has done for my lord all the good things that He has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you as ruler over Israel,
verses.25:31: that this shall not be an abomination and a stumbling block to you, to my lord—to shed innocent blood without cause and for my lord to save himself by his own hand. And may the Lord do good to my lord, and you shall remember your maidservant to do good to her."
verses.25:32: Then David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me!
verses.25:33: And blessed be your conduct, and blessed be you, who have restrained me today, on this day, from coming to bloodshed and from saving myself by my own hand.
verses.25:34: Nevertheless, as the Lord, the God of Israel lives, who has restrained me today from doing you harm, unless you had hastened and come to meet me, then I said, 'Surely there shall not be left to Nabal until the light of morning one who urinates against a wall.'"
verses.25:35: So David received from her hand all that she had brought him, and said to her, "Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and accepted your person."
verses.25:36: And Abigail came to Nabal, and behold, he had a king's drinking feast, and Nabal's heart was merry within him, and he was exceedingly drunk; so she did not report to him a word, small or great, until the light of morning.
verses.25:37: And it came to pass in the morning, when Nabal had sobered up from the wine, that his wife reported these words, and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
verses.25:38: And it came to pass after about ten days that the Lord struck Nabal, and he died.
verses.25:39: And David heard and said, "Blessed be the Lord, who has judged the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has preserved His servant from the hand of evil; and the wickedness of Nabal the Lord has returned upon his own head." And David sent and spoke concerning Abigail, to take her to himself as a wife.
verses.25:40: And the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, saying, "David has sent us to you, to take you to himself as a wife."
verses.25:41: Then she arose and bowed down to the earth upon her face, and said, "Behold, let your maidservant be a handmaid to wash the feet of your servants."
verses.25:42: So Abigail arose and mounted the donkey, and five maidens followed her; and she went after the servants of David, and became his wife.
verses.25:43: David also took Ahinoam from Israel, and both of them were his wives.
verses.25:44: But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti the son of Amis, who was from Romma.
verses.26:1: Then the Ziphites came from the parched land to Saul at the hill, saying, "Behold, David is hiding himself with us on the hill of Chelmath, which faces Jessemou."
verses.26:2: And Saul arose and went down into the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.26:3: And Saul encamped on the hill of Echela, facing Jessemou, by the road; and David dwelt in the wilderness, and David saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
verses.26:4: And David sent out spies, and knew that Saul had come ready from Keilah.
verses.26:5: And David arose secretly and came into the place where Saul was sleeping, and Abner the son of Ner, the commander of his army, was there; and Saul was sleeping in a covered chariot, and the people were encamped around him.
verses.26:6: And David answered and said to Abimelech the Hittite and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, "Who will go in with me to Saul into the camp?" And Abishai said, "I will go in with you."
verses.26:7: So David and Abishai went in among the people by night; and behold, Saul was fast asleep in a covered chariot, with his spear thrust into the ground by his head, and Abner and his people were sleeping around him.
verses.26:8: Then Abishai said to David, "Today the Lord has shut up your enemy into your hands; and now I will strike him with the spear to the ground once, and I will not strike him a second time."
verses.26:9: And David said to Abishai, "Do not bring him low; for who can stretch out his hand against the anointed of the Lord and be guiltless?"
verses.26:10: And David said, "As the Lord lives, surely the Lord will chasten him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be taken away.
verses.26:11: Far be it from me, before the Lord, to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the Lord! And now, please take the spear from by his head and the jug of water, and let us depart by ourselves."
verses.26:12: So David took the spear and the jug of water from by his head, and they departed by themselves; and no one saw, and no one knew, and no one awoke, for they were all asleep, because a stupor from the Lord had fallen upon them.
verses.26:13: Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain afar off, and great was the distance between them.
verses.26:14: And David called out to the people, and spoke to Abner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" And he said, "Who are you who calls?"
verses.26:15: And David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then do you not guard your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy the king your lord.
verses.26:16: And this thing that you have done is not good. As the Lord lives, you are sons of death, you who guard the king your lord, the anointed of the Lord! And now see where the king's spear and the jug of water are—those things that were by his head."
verses.26:17: Then Saul recognized the voice of David and said, "Is this your voice, my child David?" And David said, "Your servant, my lord, O king."
verses.26:18: And he said, "Why does my lord thus pursue after his servant? For how have I sinned, and what unrighteousness has been found in me?
verses.26:19: And now let my lord the king hear the word of his servant: if God stirs you up against me, may He smell the savor of your sacrifice; but if the sons of men, cursed are they before the Lord, for they have cast me out today from being established in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'
verses.26:20: And now do not let my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord; for the king of Israel has come out to seek my life, just as the night owl hunts in the mountains."
verses.26:21: Then Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, my child David; for I will do you no harm, because my life was precious in your eyes; and on this day I have acted foolishly and erred exceedingly."
verses.26:22: And David answered and said, "Behold, the king's spear! Let one of the young men cross over and take it.
verses.26:23: And the Lord will render to each man his righteous deeds and his faithfulness; for the Lord delivered you today into my hands, and I was not willing to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the Lord.
verses.26:24: And behold, as your life was magnified on this very day in my eyes, so may my life be magnified before the Lord, and may He shelter me, and He shall deliver me out of every affliction."
verses.26:25: Then Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my child; you shall surely accomplish what you do, and you shall surely prevail." So David departed to his place, and Saul returned to his way.
verses.27:1: And David spoke in his heart, saying, "Now one day I shall be delivered into the hands of Saul; and there is nothing good for me unless I escape safely into the land of the Philistines, and Saul ceases from seeking me within every border of Israel, and I shall be saved out of his hand."
verses.27:2: So David arose, and the four hundred men who were with him, and went to Achish the son of Ammach, king of Gath.
verses.27:3: And David dwelt with Achish, he and his men, each man and his household, even David and both his wives, Ahinoam the Israelitess and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.27:4: And it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath; so he did not continue to seek him any longer.
verses.27:5: Then David said to Achish, "If now your servant has found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the cities of the countryside, and I will dwell there; for why does your servant dwell in a royal city with you?"
verses.27:6: So he gave him Ziklag on that day; therefore Ziklag has belonged to the king of Judea to this day.
verses.27:7: And the number of the days that David dwelt along the way of the Philistines was four months.
verses.27:8: And David and his men went up and raided all the Geshurites and the Amalekites; and behold, the land was inhabited from the bordering fortified places—that region from Gelampsur—even as far as Egypt.
verses.27:9: And he struck the land, and left neither man nor woman alive; and he took flocks and herds, and donkeys and camels, and apparel, and they returned and came to Achish.
verses.27:10: Then Achish said to David, "Against whom have you raided today?" And David said to Achish, "Against the south of Judea, and against the south of Jesmega, and against the south of the Kenezite."
verses.27:11: And neither man nor woman did I leave alive to bring into Gath, saying, "Lest they report in Gath against us, saying, 'Thus David does.'" And this was his custom all the days that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines.
verses.27:12: And David was greatly trusted by Achish, who said, "He has been utterly put to shame among his people, in Israel; therefore he shall be my servant forever."
verses.28:1: Now it came to pass in those days that the Philistines gathered together in their camps to go out to fight against Israel; and Achish said to David, "Know for certain that you shall go out with me to war, you and your men."
verses.28:2: And David said to Achish, "So now you shall know what your servant will do." And Achish said to David, "Therefore I will make you chief of my bodyguard all the days."
verses.28:3: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had lamented for him and buried him in Armathaim, in his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the diviners from the land.
verses.28:4: Then the Philistines gathered together, and came and encamped at Soman; and Saul gathered together every man of Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa.
verses.28:5: And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart was exceedingly dismayed.
verses.28:6: And Saul inquired through the Lord, and the Lord did not answer him, either by dreams, or by the manifestations, or by the prophets.
verses.28:7: Then Saul said to his servants, "Seek for me a woman who is a medium, and I will go to her and inquire through her." And his servants said to him, "Behold, there is a woman who is a medium in Aeldor."
verses.28:8: So Saul disguised himself and put on other garments, and went, he and two men with him; and they came to the woman by night, and he said to her, "Please divine for me by the familiar spirit, and bring up for me whomever I shall tell you."
verses.28:9: And the woman said to him, "Behold now, you know all that Saul has done, how he has utterly destroyed the mediums and the diviners from the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to put it to death?"
verses.28:10: And Saul swore to her, saying, "As the Lord lives, no guilt shall come upon you in this matter."
verses.28:11: Then the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" And he said, "Bring up Samuel for me."
verses.28:12: And the woman saw Samuel and cried out with a loud voice; and the woman said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? For you are Saul!"
verses.28:13: And the king said to her, "Do not be afraid; tell me whom you have seen." And she said to him, "I have seen gods ascending out of the earth."
verses.28:14: And he said to her, "What did you perceive?" And she said to him, "An upright man ascending out of the earth, and he is wrapped in a double cloak." And Saul knew that this was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground and bowed down to him.
verses.28:15: Then Samuel said, "Why have you troubled me, that I should come up?" And Saul said, "I am exceedingly distressed, for the Philistines are waging war against me, and God has departed from me and no longer listens to me, either by the hand of the prophets or by dreams; and now I have called you, to make known to me what I shall do."
verses.28:16: And Samuel said, "Why do you inquire of me, seeing that the Lord has departed from you and is with your neighbor?
verses.28:17: And the Lord has done to you just as the Lord spoke by my hand; and the Lord will tear your kingdom out of your hand and give it to your neighbor, to David.
verses.28:18: Because you did not obey the voice of the Lord nor execute the fierceness of His wrath upon Amalek, therefore the Lord has done this thing to you on this day.
verses.28:19: And the Lord will deliver Israel with you into the hands of the Philistines; and tomorrow you and your sons with you shall fall, and the Lord will give the camp of Israel into the hands of the Philistines."
verses.28:20: Then Saul immediately fell at his full height upon the ground, and was exceedingly afraid because of the words of Samuel; and there was no strength left in him, for he had not eaten bread all that day and all that night.
verses.28:21: And the woman came in to Saul and saw that he was exceedingly agitated; and she said to him, "Behold now, your maidservant has obeyed your voice, and I have placed my life in my hand, and have heeded the words which you spoke to me.
verses.28:22: Now therefore, please listen to the voice of your maidservant, and I will set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, that there may be strength in you, for you shall go on your way."
verses.28:23: But he refused to eat. Yet his servants and the woman strongly urged him, and he listened to their voice; so he arose from the ground and sat upon the seat.
verses.28:24: Now the woman had a pasture-fed heifer in the house; and she hastened and slaughtered it, and she took flour and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread,
verses.28:25: and she brought it before Saul and before his servants; and they ate, and they arose and departed that night.
verses.29:1: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek, and Israel encamped in Aeddon, which is in Israel.
verses.29:2: And the lords of the Philistines marched past by hundreds and by thousands, while David and his men marched past in the rear with Achish.
verses.29:3: Then the lords of the Philistines said, "Who are these who are passing through?" And Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel? He has been with us for days—this is the second year—and I have found nothing in him from the day he defected to me even to this day."
verses.29:4: But the commanders of the Philistines were displeased with him, and they said to him, "Send the man back to his place where you stationed him, and let him not go with us to the battle, and let him not become a plotter against the camp. For with what would this man reconcile himself to his lord? Would it not be with the heads of those men?
verses.29:5: Is this not David, of whom they led the song in dances, saying, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
verses.29:6: Then Achish called David and said to him, "As the Lord lives, surely you are upright and good in my eyes, as are your going out and your coming in with me in the camp; for I have found no evil against you from the day you came to me until this present day, and in the eyes of the lords you are good.
verses.29:7: Now therefore, turn back and go in peace, and you shall do no evil in the eyes of the lords of the Philistines."
verses.29:8: And David said to Achish, "What have I done to you, and what have you found in your servant from the day I have been before you even to this day, that I should not go to fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"
verses.29:9: And Achish answered David, "I know that you are good in my eyes; yet the lords of the Philistines say, 'He shall not go with us to battle.'
verses.29:10: Now therefore, rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who have come with you, and go to the place where I stationed you; and do not set a wicked word in your heart, for you are good before me. Rise early on the way, and as soon as it is light for you, depart."
verses.29:11: So David rose early, he and his men, to depart and to guard the land of the Philistines; and the Philistines went up to make war against Israel.
verses.30:1: Now it came to pass, when David and his men entered Keilah on the third day, that Amalek had made a raid against the South and against Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire;
verses.30:2: and the women and all that were in it, from small to great—they did not put to death either man or woman, but carried them away captive and went on their way.
verses.30:3: And David and his men came to the city, and behold, it was burned with fire, and their wives, their sons, and their daughters had been carried away captive.
verses.30:4: Then David and his men lifted up their voice and wept, until there was no longer strength in them to weep.
verses.30:5: And both of David's wives had been taken captive: Ahinoam the Israelite, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.30:6: Now David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was deeply grieved, each man for his sons and for his daughters; yet David was strengthened in the Lord his God.
verses.30:7: And David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, "Bring the ephod near."
verses.30:8: Then David inquired through the Lord, saying, "Shall I pursue after this raiding band? Shall I overtake them?" And He said to him, "Pursue, for you shall surely overtake them, and you shall surely rescue them."
verses.30:9: So David went, he and the four hundred men with him, and they came to the Brook Besor; and the rest halted.
verses.30:10: And the rest pursued with four hundred men, while two hundred men stayed behind, who sat down on the other side of the Brook Besor.
verses.30:11: Then they found an Egyptian man in the field, and they took him and brought him to David in the field; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
verses.30:12: And they gave him a piece of a fig cake and he ate, and his spirit was restored within him; for he had not eaten bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights.
verses.30:13: And David said to him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?" And the Egyptian young man said, "I am the servant of an Amalekite man, and my master left me behind because I fell ill three days ago today.
verses.30:14: And we made a raid upon the south of Cholthi, and upon the regions of Judea, and upon Gilboa, and we burned Ziklag with fire."
verses.30:15: Then David said to him, "Will you lead me down to this raiding band?" And he said, "Swear now to me by God that you will not put me to death and will not deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will lead you down to this raiding band."
verses.30:16: So he led him down there; and behold, they were spread abroad over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and feasting over all the great spoil which they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
verses.30:17: And David came upon them and struck them down from dawn until evening and on the next day; and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who mounted camels and fled.
verses.30:18: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued both of his wives.
verses.30:19: And nothing of theirs was missing, from small to great, from the spoil even to sons and daughters, and to everything they had taken from them; David brought back all.
verses.30:20: And he took all the flocks and the herds and drove them ahead of the spoil; and of that spoil it was said, "This is the spoil of David."
verses.30:21: Now David came to the two hundred men who had grown too weary to follow after David, whom he had seated by the Brook Beana; and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. And David drew near to the people, and they asked him concerning his welfare.
verses.30:22: Then every pestilent and wicked man among the men of war who had gone with David answered and said, "Because they did not pursue with us, we will not give them any of the spoil which we have rescued, except that each man may take away his wife and his children and depart."
verses.30:23: But David said, "You shall not do so after the Lord has given to us and preserved us, and the Lord has delivered the raiding band that came against us into our hands.
verses.30:24: And who will heed these words of yours? For they are no less than you; for as is the share of him who goes down to battle, so shall be the share of him who stays by the baggage; they shall share alike."
verses.30:25: And so it was from that day forward, that it became a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
verses.30:26: Now David came to Ziklag, and he sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah and to his neighbors, saying, "Behold, from the spoil of the enemies of the Lord"—
verses.30:27: to those in Bethsur, and to those in Ramah of the South, and to those in Geththor,
verses.30:28: and to those in Aroer, and to those of Ammadi, and to those in Saphi, and to those in Esthie,
verses.30:29: and to those in Gath, and to those in Kimath, and to those in Saphek, and to those in Thimath, and to those in Carmel, and to those in the cities of Israel, and to those in the cities of Kenezi,
verses.30:30: and to those in Jerimuth, and to those in Beersheba, and to those in Noo,
verses.30:31: and to those in Hebron, and to all the places through which David had passed, he and his men.
verses.31:1: Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell wounded on Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:2: And the Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, and Jonadab, and Malchishua, the son of Saul.
verses.31:3: And the battle grew heavy against Saul, and the javelin-throwers, men who were archers, found him, and he was wounded in the flanks.
verses.31:4: Then Saul said to his armorbearer, "Draw your sword and pierce me through with it, lest these uncircumcised ones come and pierce me through and mock me." But his armorbearer was not willing, for he was greatly afraid. Therefore Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
verses.31:5: And when his armorbearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died with him.
verses.31:6: Thus Saul and his three sons and his armorbearer died on that day together.
verses.31:7: And when the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley, and those who were on the other side of the Jordan, saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook their cities and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
verses.31:8: And it came to pass on the next day, that the Philistines came to strip the dead; and they found Saul and his three sons fallen on the mountains of Gilboa.
verses.31:9: And they turned him over and stripped off his armor, and sent it throughout the land of the Philistines all around, proclaiming the glad tidings to their idols and to the people.
verses.31:10: And they placed his armor in the temple of Astarte, and his body they fastened on the wall of Bethem.
verses.31:11: And the inhabitants of Jabesh of Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul.
verses.31:12: And every valiant man arose and journeyed all night, and they took the body of Saul and the body of Jonathan his son from the wall of Bethsam, and brought them to Jabesh and burned them there.
verses.31:13: And they took their bones and buried them beneath the field of Jabesh, and fasted seven days. And it came to pass after the death of Saul, that David returned from striking down Amalek, and David stayed in Ziklag two days.

notes.1:1: The Greek preserves distinct forms for the place and ancestral names: Armathaim Sipha (MT: Ramathaim-zophim), Jeremeel (MT: Jeroham), Thoke (MT: Tohu), and "in Nasib of Ephraim" (MT: "son of Zuph, an Ephraimite").
notes.1:5: The Greek text states that Elkanah gave Hannah "one portion" (MT: "a double portion"), and in verse 6 attributes her despondency directly to her barrenness rather than provocation by Peninnah.
notes.1:11: Greek "Adonai, Lord Eloi Sabaoth" transliterates Hebrew divine titles ("Sabaoth" meaning "of hosts"); the LXX also explicitly includes the Nazirite vow to abstain from wine and strong drink.
notes.1:14: In the Greek text, Eli's young servant rebukes Hannah rather than Eli himself, and in verse 15 Hannah describes herself as "a woman whose day is hard" (MT: "a woman of sorrowful spirit").
notes.1:24: The Greek reads "a three-year-old calf" (MT: "three bulls"), and verse 28 ends chapter 1 with "And she said:" to introduce Hannah's prayer in 2:1.
notes.2:5: Greek "those who were weak have forsaken the land" reflects a distinctive LXX rendering of the clause concerning the hungry ceasing to labor.
notes.2:10: The Greek text includes an expanded exhortation (paralleling Jeremiah 9:23-24) against boasting in prudence, might, or riches, and reads "our kings" in the plural.
notes.2:18: Greek "ephoud bar" transcribes the Hebrew phrase for a linen ephod.
notes.2:22: The Greek text omits the clause found in the MT regarding Eli's sons lying with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
notes.2:29: The Greek reads "with a shameless eye" and "to bless yourselves" (MT: "kick at" and "fatten yourselves"), and in verse 31 reads "your seed" (MT: "your arm").
notes.3:3: Greek reads "before the lamp of God was trimmed" (episkeuasthenai), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "before the lamp of God went out."
notes.3:13: Greek reads "reviling God" (kakologountes theon), preserving an ancient reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "bringing a curse upon themselves."
notes.3:14: Greek reads "with incense and with sacrifices," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "with sacrifice or offering."
notes.3:21: The Greek text includes an expanded conclusion affirming Samuel's accreditation across all Israel and contrasting him with the aged Eli and his wicked sons.
notes.4:1: Greek allophyloi ("foreigners") is the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines throughout 1–4 Kingdoms.
notes.4:12: Greek Iemeinaios ("Jeminite") denotes a man of the tribe of Benjamin.
notes.4:15: Greek gives Eli's age as ninety years and adds his question to the men standing around him, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text gives ninety-eight years.
notes.4:18: Greek states that Eli's back was broken (Hebrew: his neck) and that he had judged Israel twenty years (Hebrew Masoretic Text: forty years).
notes.4:21: Greek renders the child's name as Ouai Barchaboth ("Woe Barchaboth") rather than the Hebrew Ichabod, and in verse 22 attributes the lament to a plural subject ("they said").
notes.5:1: Greek reads Abenner here instead of Ebenezer (as in 4:1), and uses the Greek name Azotus for Ashdod throughout the chapter.
notes.5:4: Greek renders "threshold" with a transliteration of the Hebrew term (hammiphtan) and preserves a double description of Dagon's severed palms and wrists, leaving only his spine.
notes.5:6: Greek uniquely states that the affliction broke out "in the ships" (eis tas naus) and that mice sprang up in the midst of the land.
notes.5:9: Greek uses hedrai ("seats" or "sitting parts") both for the afflicted body parts ("secret parts" in verses 3, 9, and 12) and for the "seats" the Gittites made for themselves.
notes.5:10: Greek reads Ashkelon and the Ashkelonites, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Ekron and the Ekronites.
notes.6:3: The Greek uses basanos ("torment") for the reparation offering throughout chapter 6 (vv. 3, 4, 8, 17) and reads "atonement shall be made for you" where the Masoretic Text has "it will be known to you."
notes.6:4: Greek hedras literally means "seats," a euphemism for the afflicted parts or tumors; the Greek also uses satrapai ("lords" or "satraps") for the Philistine rulers.
notes.6:8: The Greek text preserves the negative reading "you shall not put" (ou thesete) and transliterates the Hebrew coffer term as berechthan here and ergab in vv. 11 and 15.
notes.6:14: The Septuagint reads "Hosea" (also in v. 18) where the Masoretic Text has "Joshua," and states actively that they "set up a great stone" beside the cart.
notes.6:19: The Septuagint uniquely specifies that "the sons of Jeconiah were not pleased with the men of Beth-shemesh"; similarly, v. 16 names Ashkelon rather than Ekron, and v. 18 reads "village of the Perizzite" instead of "unwalled village."
notes.7:1: The Septuagint reads "Amminadab" (Ameinadab) where the Masoretic Text has "Abinadab."
notes.7:9: The Septuagint reads "with all the people" (syn panti to lao) where the Masoretic Text has "wholly" or "as a whole burnt offering."
notes.7:12: Where the Masoretic Text names the place Shen, the Septuagint translates "the Old" (tes palaias), and gives Ebenezer both as a transliteration and in translation ("Stone of the Helper").
notes.7:14: The Septuagint reads "from Ashkelon to Azob" where the Masoretic Text has "from Ekron to Gath," and in v. 16 describes the circuit sites as "sanctified places."
notes.8:4: The Septuagint reads "the men of Israel" rather than "all the elders of Israel," and uses the dual form Ramathaim (Harmathaim, as in 7:17) for Samuel's hometown of Ramah.
notes.8:12: The Septuagint specifies "commanders of hundreds" (rather than fifties) and "to reap his harvest and gather his vintage" (rather than plowing and reaping).
notes.8:16: The Septuagint reads "your herds and your good things" where the Masoretic Text has "your finest young men," and states that the king will "take a tenth" for his work.
notes.9:1: Greek names Saul's ancestors Ared, Bachi, and Aphek (differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's Zeror, Becorath, and Aphiah), and in 9:4 reads the place names Selcha, Easakem, and Jakim.
notes.9:2: Greek reads "taller than all the land" (hyper pasan ten gen) where the Masoretic Text reads "all the people."
notes.9:12: Greek transliterates Hebrew bamah ("high place") as the place name Bama throughout chapters 9 to 11.
notes.9:22: Greek numbers the invited guests at "about seventy men" (MT: "about thirty men").
notes.9:24: Greek has the cook "boiled" (hepsesen) the thigh and Samuel describe it as set aside "as a testimony above the others—cut off pieces," and in 9:25 reads that "they spread a bed for Saul on the housetop, and he lay down to sleep."
notes.10:1: Greek preserves Samuel's fuller declaration of Saul's rule, deliverance of Israel, and the sign of his anointing, which is shorter in the Masoretic Text.
notes.10:2: Greek reads "leaping greatly" (hallomenous megala) where the Masoretic Text has the place name Zelzah.
notes.10:5: Greek contains a doublet for Hebrew netsiv pelishtim, translating it both as "the garrison of the foreigners" and as "Nasib the foreigner"; here and in 9:16 Greek uses allophyloi ("foreigners") for the Philistines.
notes.10:8: Greek reads "before Gilead" (emprosthen tes Galaad) where the Masoretic Text has "before me to Gilgal."
notes.10:24: Greek reads "all the people recognized him" (egnosan) rather than "all the people shouted" as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.11:1: Greek begins with "about a month later" (hos meta mena), matching Dead Sea Scrolls evidence, whereas the Masoretic Text lacks this phrase and ends 10:27 with Saul holding his peace.
notes.11:5: Greek reads "after the morning" (meta to proi), reading the Hebrew consonants as "morning" rather than "oxen" as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.11:8: Greek names the muster site "Abiezek in Bama" and numbers Israel at six hundred thousand and Judah at seventy thousand (MT: Bezek; three hundred thousand and thirty thousand).
notes.11:13: Greek attributes the refusal to execute anyone to Samuel rather than Saul (MT), and in 11:15 likewise states that Samuel anointed Saul as king, offered the sacrifices, and rejoiced with all Israel.
notes.12:2: Greek kathesomai literally means "I shall sit," contrasting Samuel's retirement with the king going about before the people (where the Hebrew text reads "I am gray-headed").
notes.12:3: The Greek text reads "a bribe [lit. propitiation] and a sandal" (exilasma kai hypodema), a distinctive Septuagint reading echoing Amos 2:6 and Sirach 46:19 where the Hebrew speaks of a ransom to blind the eyes.
notes.12:9: The Greek names the king of Hazor as Jabis (Iabeis, corresponding to Jabin) and renders the Philistines here and throughout this book as "foreigners" (allophyloi, literally "people of another tribe").
notes.12:11: The Septuagint lists Jeroboam (where the Hebrew reads Jerubbaal, i.e., Gideon) and Barak (where the Hebrew reads Bedan).
notes.12:25: Greek prostethesesthe literally means "you shall be added," carrying the biblical idiom of being gathered away in death (reflecting the Hebrew root for adding rather than sweeping away).
notes.13:3: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew word for "garrison/prefect" as a personal name, Nasib, translates Geba as "the hill," and reads Saul's proclamation as "The slaves have rebelled!" (where the Hebrew reads "Let the Hebrews hear!").
notes.13:15: The Septuagint preserves the full narrative of Samuel departing from Gilgal and the remnant following Saul to Gibeah of Benjamin, a passage omitted by scribal error in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:18: "Gai of Samein" transliterates the Septuagint's distinctive place name Gai ten Samein (corresponding to the Valley of Zeboim in the Hebrew text).
notes.13:21: In this difficult verse, the Septuagint speaks of the vintage being ready for harvest and gives a fixed sharpening rate of three shekels per tooth (or prong), with the same standing rate for the ax and the sickle.
notes.13:23: The closing clause, "and he did not tell his father," stands at the end of 13:23 in the Septuagint (anticipating Jonathan's action in 14:1, where the clause appears in the Hebrew text).
notes.14:1: The Greek text transliterates the Hebrew word for "garrison/outpost" as a place name, "Messab" here and "Messaph" in 14:6, 11, 12, and 15. Other distinctive Septuagint proper names in the opening verses include Magon (v. 2), Jochabel and Levi (v. 3), and Bazes and Sennaar (v. 4).
notes.14:14: The Septuagint reads "with darts and pebbles of the field," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes an area of land ("within about half a furrow of an acre of land").
notes.14:18: The Greek text reads "the ephod" twice here (consistent with Ahijah bearing the ephod in 14:3), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the ark of God."
notes.14:41: The Septuagint preserves a longer prayer of Saul invoking the Urim ("clear signs," Greek delous) and Thummim ("holiness," Greek hosioteta), following the distinctive Greek reading "for servitude" in 14:40.
notes.14:48: "Aunanein" renders an obscure untranslated word unique to the Codex Vaticanus Greek text. Other Septuagint-distinct names in the closing summary include Baitheor (v. 47), Jessiul (v. 49), Ahinaas and Neri (v. 50), and Jamin and Abier (v. 51).
notes.15:3: The Greek reads "Jerim" as a proper name (also in 15:8), reflecting a transliteration of the Hebrew term for devoting to destruction.
notes.15:7: The Greek reads "Asshur" (Assyria) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Shur."
notes.15:23: The Greek renders the Hebrew word for household idols (terafim) with the similar-sounding Greek word therapeia ("healing" or "service"), producing the clause "grief and toil bring on healing."
notes.15:29: The Greek reads "Israel shall be divided in two," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to "the Glory [or Strength] of Israel."
notes.15:34: "Armathaim" is the distinctive Septuagint name corresponding to Ramah (Ramathaim) in the Hebrew text (also in 16:13).
notes.16:8: The Greek reads "Amminadab" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Abinadab."
notes.16:12: The Greek specifies that David was pleasing in appearance "to the Lord," names David directly in the Lord's command, and states "for this one is good."
notes.16:14: The Greek verb literally means "to choke" or "suffocate" (also in 16:15), vividly expressing the torment caused by the evil spirit.
notes.16:20: The Greek reads "a homer of bread" (a dry measure), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants rendered "a donkey laden with bread" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.17:1: The Greek calls the Philistines allophyloi (literally "foreigners"), its standard designation for them in 1-4 Kingdoms, and reads "Socoh of Idumea" and "Ephermem" where the Masoretic Text has "Socoh, which belongs to Judah" and "Ephes-dammim."
notes.17:3: The Greek reads kyklo ("with a circle"), likely an early Greek textual variation for koilas ("valley").
notes.17:4: The Greek gives Goliath's height as "four cubits and a span" (agreeing with 4QSam-a and Josephus), rather than the Masoretic Text's "six cubits and a span."
notes.17:32: Following the shorter Old Greek text, verses 12-31, 41, and 50 are not present in this chapter, nor are 17:55-18:5.
notes.17:43: The Greek adds "and stones" to Goliath's taunt and preserves David's reply, "No, but worse than a dog," which does not appear in the Masoretic Text.
notes.18:20: Greek Melchol is the regular Septuagint spelling of Michal; verses 10-11 and 17-19 are not present in the shorter Old Greek text.
notes.18:21: The Greek concludes the verse with "And the hand of the Philistines was upon Saul," where the Masoretic Text records Saul telling David a second time that he would become his son-in-law.
notes.18:27: The Greek reports that David struck down "one hundred men," matching Saul's demand in verse 25, whereas the Masoretic Text reads "two hundred men."
notes.19:5: Greek allophylos ("foreigner") is the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines; the Greek also reads "and all Israel saw and rejoiced" rather than addressing Saul directly as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.19:9: The Greek reads katheudon ("sleeping"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "sitting."
notes.19:13: The Greek renders the household images (teraphim) as kenotaphia ("cenotaphs," i.e., funerary effigies) and reads "a liver of goats" (hepar ton aigon) rather than "a pillow of goat's hair."
notes.19:18: The Septuagint distinguishes "Ramathaim" (Greek Harmathaim) from "Auath in Ramah," the latter corresponding to "Naioth in Ramah" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.19:22: The Greek reads "the well of the threshing floor that is in Sephei," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "the great well that is in Secu."
notes.20:3: The Greek reads "the space between me and death is filled up" (empeplestai), reflecting a different reading from the Hebrew idiom "there is but a step between me and death."
notes.20:16: The Greek syntax of verses 15–16 ("may the name of Jonathan be found out from the house of David") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's statement that Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David.
notes.20:19: "Ergab" (and "Argab" in verse 41) transliterates a Hebrew term for a mound or cairn, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the stone Ezel" (v. 19) and "from beside the south" (v. 41).
notes.20:20: "Harmattarei" transliterates the Hebrew word for "target" as a proper name; in verse 21, "arrow" translates the rare Greek transliteration gouzan (Hebrew chets), while "arrows" elsewhere in the chapter renders schizai (lit. "splinters" or "shafts").
notes.20:30: The Greek reads "Son of deserting maidens" (korasion automolounton), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "Son of a perverse, rebellious woman."
notes.21:2: The Greek text reads Abimelech (corresponding to Hebrew Ahimelech) and Nomba (for Nob) throughout these chapters.
notes.21:3: Greek renders the Hebrew idiom for an unnamed place doubly, translating it as "Faithfulness of God" and transliterating it as the place name Phellani Maemoni.
notes.21:8: Greek doubly renders the Hebrew word for "detained" with a Greek participle and the transliteration Neessaran, and reads "Doeg the Syrian, tending the mules of Saul" where the Hebrew reads "Doeg the Edomite, chief of Saul's herdsmen."
notes.21:10: Throughout 1 Kingdoms, the Septuagint translates the Hebrew term for Philistines as allophyloi ("foreigners"). Here the Greek also does not include "behind the ephod."
notes.22:5: Greek reads "in the city of Sarik," whereas the Hebrew text reads "in the forest of Hereth."
notes.22:6: Greek reads "below the field that is in Bamah," whereas the Hebrew text reads "under the tamarisk tree in Ramah."
notes.22:18: The Greek text numbers the slain priests at three hundred and five men, whereas the Hebrew text reads eighty-five.
notes.22:23: Greek reads "wherever I seek a place for my own life, I will seek one for your life also," whereas the Hebrew text reads "he who seeks my life seeks your life."
notes.23:2: This Greek text reads "and you shall strike Keilah" (likely by assimilation to the preceding verb), whereas the Hebrew text reads "and save Keilah."
notes.23:11: This Greek text compresses verses 11 and 12 (omitting verse 12) and uses the verb apokleio ("shut up" or "deliver up").
notes.23:13: The Greek text reads "about four hundred" men with David, whereas the Hebrew text reads "about six hundred."
notes.23:15: Greek Kaine (literally "New," also in verses 16, 18, and 19) reflects reading Hebrew Horesh as hadashah ("new").
notes.23:26: Greek describes David as "taking cover" while Saul and his men "encamped against" him, where the Hebrew text reads "hurrying" and "closing in on."
notes.24:3: The Septuagint renders the place name as Eddaiem, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Rocks of the Wild Goats."
notes.24:4: Greek paraskeuasasthai ("to prepare himself") is the Septuagint's modest euphemism for relieving oneself, corresponding to the Hebrew idiom "to cover his feet."
notes.24:20: The Septuagint reads a conditional statement including "in distress" (en thlipsei), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text frames the clause as a rhetorical question.
notes.24:23: The Septuagint preserves the proper name Messara ("the narrow pass of Messara"), corresponding to the common noun "the stronghold" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.25:1: The Septuagint reads Ramathaim (Greek Harmathaim, the dual form) rather than "Ramah," and places David in the wilderness of Maon (Greek Maan) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Paran."
notes.25:3: Greek kynikos ("dog-like") reflects reading the Hebrew consonants as kelev ("dog") rather than the gentilic "Calebite" found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.25:22: The Septuagint preserves the direct self-imprecation "to David," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the scribal euphemism "to the enemies of David."
notes.25:43: The Septuagint reads "from Israel" (ex Israel), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from Jezreel."
notes.25:44: The Septuagint gives the proper names Amis (Greek Ameis) and Romma, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Laish" and "Gallim."
notes.26:1: Greek adds "from the parched land" and "with us," and reads "Chelmath" (and "Echela" in v. 3) facing "Jessemou," corresponding to Hebrew Hachilah facing Jeshimon.
notes.26:4: Greek reads "ready from Keilah," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "for a certainty."
notes.26:5: Greek lampene denotes a covered chariot or royal wagon (also in v. 7), where the Hebrew refers to the camp enclosure; in v. 6, Greek also reads "Abimelech" rather than Hebrew "Ahimelech."
notes.26:16: Greek has the ironic positive participle "you who guard" rather than the Hebrew negative "because you have not guarded."
notes.26:20: Greek reads "to seek my life, just as the night owl hunts in the mountains," whereas the Hebrew reads "to seek a single flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains."
notes.27:1: Throughout chapters 27–28, "Philistines" renders Greek allophyloi (literally "foreigners"), the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines in 1 Kingdoms.
notes.27:2: Greek reads "four hundred men" (Hebrew "six hundred") and "Ammach" (Hebrew "Maoch"); in v. 3, Ahinoam is called "the Israelitess" rather than "the Jezreelitess."
notes.27:7: Greek reads "along the way of the Philistines" for "four months," whereas the Hebrew reads "in the country of the Philistines" for "a year [lit. days] and four months."
notes.27:8: The Greek phrase rendered "from the bordering fortified places—that region from Gelampsur" is syntactically difficult and preserves a conflated place name (Gelampsur) where the Hebrew speaks of ancient inhabitants toward Shur; Greek also omits the Girzites.
notes.27:10: Greek reads "Jesmega" and "the Kenezite" (Hebrew "the Jerahmeelites" and "the Kenites"); in v. 11, the Greek verb shifts abruptly into the first-person singular ("did I leave alive").
notes.28:3: Greek reads "Armathaim" (corresponding to Hebrew Ramah); in v. 4, "Soman" corresponds to Shunem, and in v. 7, "Aeldor" corresponds to En Dor.
notes.28:6: Greek delois ("manifestations" or "revelations") is the Septuagint's regular rendering for the Hebrew priestly Urim.
notes.28:14: Greek reads "What did you perceive?" and "An upright man," whereas the Hebrew reads "What is his form?" and "An old man."
notes.28:16: Greek reads "and is with your neighbor" (referring to David, as in v. 17), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "and has become your adversary."
notes.28:19: Greek reads "tomorrow you and your sons with you shall fall," whereas the Hebrew reads "tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me."
notes.29:1: The Greek text reads 'Aeddon, which is in Israel,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'the spring which is in Jezreel.' Throughout 1 Kingdoms, the Greek renders 'Philistines' with a term literally meaning 'foreigners.'
notes.29:3: The Greek reads 'these who are passing through' (interpreting the Hebrew word for 'Hebrews' as a participle meaning 'passing over') and specifies 'this is the second year' for David's stay.
notes.29:6: The Greek text lacks the negative found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text ('you are not good in the eyes of the lords'), reading positively 'in the eyes of the lords you are good.'
notes.29:11: The Greek reads 'to guard the land of the Philistines' and 'to make war against Israel,' whereas the Hebrew reads 'to return to the land of the Philistines' and 'went up to Jezreel.'
notes.30:1: The Greek text names 'Keilah' as the city David entered, whereas the Hebrew reads 'Ziklag' in both halves of the verse.
notes.30:8: 'Raiding band' translates the Greek loanword geddour, a transliteration of the Hebrew term for a marauding troop (recurring in verses 15 and 23).
notes.30:9: The Greek reads 'four hundred men' here rather than 'six hundred' as in the Hebrew, while verse 10 continues with four hundred pursuing and two hundred remaining by the Brook Besor.
notes.30:14: The Greek reads 'Cholthi' and 'Gilboa' where the Hebrew reads 'Cherethites' and 'the Negev of Caleb.'
notes.30:27: In verses 27–30, the Greek list of cities diverges substantially from the Hebrew, naming Bethsur, Geththor, Ammadi, Saphi, Esthie, Gath, Kimath, Saphek, Thimath, Carmel, the cities of Israel and Kenezi, Jerimuth, Beersheba, and Noo (and similarly 'Brook Beana' in verse 21).
notes.31:2: The Greek reads 'Jonadab' (rather than 'Abinadab' as in the Hebrew) and retains the singular 'son of Saul' following the three names.
notes.31:3: The Greek specifies that Saul was 'wounded in the flanks' (literally the soft parts beneath the ribs), where the Hebrew refers more generally to being badly wounded or in anguish.
notes.31:9: The Greek reads 'they turned him over' rather than 'they cut off his head' as in the Hebrew; in verses 10 and 12 the city wall is named Bethem and Bethsam (Hebrew Beth-shan).
notes.31:13: The Greek reads 'beneath the field of Jabesh' (Hebrew 'under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh') and appends the opening sentence of 2 Kingdoms (2 Samuel 1:1) directly to the close of the chapter.

unplaced.text: And David arose and departed, and Jonathan entered into the city.
